8.46.d: त्वावतः पुरूवसो वयमिन्द्र प्रणेतः । स्मसि स्थातर्हरीणाम् ॥
8.46.e: WE, Indra, Lord of ample wealth, our Guide, depend on one like thee,  Thou driver of the Tawny Steeds.

8.46.d: त्वां हि सत्यमद्रिवो विद्म दातारमिषाम् । विद्म दातारं रयीणाम् ॥
8.46.e: For, Hurler of the Bolt, we know thee true, the giver of our food,  We know the giver of our wealth.

8.46.d: आ यस्य ते महिमानं शतमूते शतक्रतो । गीर्भिर्गृणन्ति कारवः ॥
8.46.e: O thou whose majesty the bards celebrate with their songs, thou Lord,  Of hundred powers and hundred aids.

8.46.d: सुनीथो घा स मर्त्यो यं मरुतो यमर्यमा । मित्रः पान्त्यद्रुहः ॥
8.46.e: Fair guidance hath the mortal man whom Aryaman, the Marut host,  And Mitra, void of guile, protect.

8.46.d: दधानो गोमदश्ववत्सुवीर्यमादित्यजूत एधते । सदा राया पुरुस्पृहा ॥
8.46.e: Kine, steeds, and hero strength he gains, and prospers, by the Ādityas sped,  Ever in wealth which all desire.

8.46.d: तमिन्द्रं दानमीमहे शवसानमभीर्वम् । ईशानं राय ईमहे ॥
8.46.e: We pray to Indra for his gift, to him the Fearless and the Strong,  We pray to him the Lord of wealth.

8.46.d: तस्मिन्हि सन्त्यूतयो विश्वा अभीरवः सचा । तमा वहन्तु सप्तयः पुरूवसुं मदाय हरयः सुतम् ॥
8.46.e: For verily combined in him are all the fearless powers of aid.  Him, rich in wealth, let swift Steeds bring to us, his Bays, to Soma juice for his carouse:

8.46.d: यस्ते मदो वरेण्यो य इन्द्र वृत्रहन्तमः । य आददिः स्व१र्नृभिर्यः पृतनासु दुष्टरः ॥
8.46.e: Yea, that most excellent carouse, Indra, which slays most enemies,  With Heroes wins the light of heaven, and is invincible in war:

8.46.d: यो दुष्टरो विश्ववार श्रवाय्यो वाजेष्वस्ति तरुता । स नः शविष्ठ सवना वसो गहि गमेम गोमति व्रजे ॥
8.46.e: Which merits fame, all-bountiful! and, unsubdued, hath victory in deeds of might.  So come to our libations, Strongest! Excellent! May we obtain a stall of kine.

8.46.d: गव्यो षु णो यथा पुराश्वयोत रथया । वरिवस्य महामह ॥
8.46.e: Responding to our wish for cows, for steeds, and chariots, as of old,  Be gracious, Greatest of the Great

8.46.d: नहि ते शूर राधसोऽन्तं विन्दामि सत्रा । दशस्या नो मघवन्नू चिदद्रिवो धियो वाजेभिराविथ ॥
8.46.e: For, Hero, nowhere can I find the bounds of thy munificence.  Still do thou favour us, O Bolt-armed Maghavan: with strength hast thou rewarded hymns.

8.46.d: य ऋष्वः श्रावयत्सखा विश्वेत्स वेद जनिमा पुरुष्टुतः । तं विश्वे मानुषा युगेन्द्रं हवन्ते तविषं यतस्रुचः ॥
8.46.e: High, glorifier of his friend, he knows all generations, he whom many praise.  All races of mankind with ladies lifted up invoke that Mighty Indra's aid.

8.46.d: स नो वाजेष्वविता पुरूवसुः पुरःस्थाता मघवा वृत्रहा भुवत् ॥
8.46.e: Be he our Champion and Protector in great deeds, rich in all wealth, the Vṛtra-slayer, Maghavan.

8.46.d: अभि वो वीरमन्धसो मदेषु गाय गिरा महा विचेतसम् । इन्द्रं नाम श्रुत्यं शाकिनं वचो यथा ॥
8.46.e: In the wild raptures of the juice sing to your Hero with high laud, to him the Wise,  To Indra, glorious in his name, the Mighty One, even as the hymn alloweth it.

8.46.d: ददी रेक्णस्तन्वे ददिर्वसु ददिर्वाजेषु पुरुहूत वाजिनम् । नूनमथ ॥
8.46.e: Thou givest wealth to me myself, thou givest treasure, Excellent! and the strong steed,  O Much-invoked, in deeds of might, yea, even now.

8.46.d: विश्वेषामिरज्यन्तं वसूनां सासह्वांसं चिदस्य वर्पसः । कृपयतो नूनमत्यथ ॥
8.46.e: Him, Sovran Ruler of all precious things, who even hath power o’er this fair form of his,  As now it taketh shape, and afterward,

8.46.d: महः सु वो अरमिषे स्तवामहे मीळ्हुषे अरंगमाय जग्मये । यज्ञेभिर्गीर्भिर्विश्वमनुषां मरुतामियक्षसि गाये त्वा नमसा गिरा ॥
8.46.e: We praise, so that the Mighty One may speed to you, Pourer of  bounties  , Traveller, prepared to go.  Thou favourest the Maruts known to all, by song and sacrifice.  With song and praise I sing to thee.

8.46.d: ये पातयन्ते अज्मभिर्गिरीणां स्नुभिरेषाम् । यज्ञं महिष्वणीनां सुम्नं तुविष्वणीनां प्राध्वरे ॥
8.46.e: We in the sacrifice perform their will whose voice is lifted high,  The worship of those Thundering Ones who o’er the ridges of these mountains fly in troops.

8.46.d: प्रभङ्गं दुर्मतीनामिन्द्र शविष्ठा भर । रयिमस्मभ्यं युज्यं चोदयन्मते ज्येष्ठं चोदयन्मते ॥
8.46.e: O Indra, Mightiest, bring us that which crushes men of evil minds,  Wealth suited to our needs, O Stirrer of the thought, best wealth, O thou who stirrest thought.

8.46.d: सनितः सुसनितरुग्र चित्र चेतिष्ठ सूनृत । प्रासहा सम्राट् सहुरिं सहन्तं भुज्युं वाजेषु पूर्व्यम् ॥
8.46.e: O Winner, noble winner, strong, wondrous, most splendid, excellent,  Sole Lord of victory, bring all-overpowering wealth, joy-giving, chief in deeds of might.

8.46.d: आ स एतु य ईवदाँ अदेवः पूर्तमाददे । यथा चिद्वशो अश्व्यः पृथुश्रवसि कानीते३ऽस्या व्युष्याददे ॥
8.46.e: Now let the godless man approach who hath received reward so great  As Vaśa, Aśvya, when this light of morning dawned, received from Pṛthuśravas, from Kanīta's son.

8.46.d: षष्टिं सहस्राश्व्यस्यायुतासनमुष्ट्रानां विंशतिं शता । दश श्यावीनां शता दश त्र्यरुषीणां दश गवां सहस्रा ॥
8.46.e: Steeds sixty thousand and ten thousand kine, and twenty hundred camels I obtained;  Ten hundred brown in hue, and other ten red in three spots: in all, ten thousand kine.

8.46.d: दश श्यावा ऋधद्रयो वीतवारास आशवः । मथ्रा नेमिं नि वावृतुः ॥
8.46.e: Ten browns that make my wealth increase, fleet steeds whose tails are long and fair,  Turn with swift whirl my chariot wheel;

8.46.d: दानासः पृथुश्रवसः कानीतस्य सुराधसः । रथं हिरण्ययं ददन्मंहिष्ठः सूरिरभूद्वर्षिष्ठमकृत श्रवः ॥
8.46.e: The gifts which Pṛthuśravas gave, Kanīta's son munificent.  He gave a chariot wrought of gold: the prince was passing bountiful, and won himself most lofty fame.

8.46.d: आ नो वायो महे तने याहि मखाय पाजसे । वयं हि ते चकृमा भूरि दावने सद्यश्चिन्महि दावने ॥
8.46.e: Come thou to this great rite of ours, Vāyu! to give us vigorous light.  We have served thee that thou mightest give much to us, yea, mightest quickly give great wealth.

8.46.d: यो अश्वेभिर्वहते वस्त उस्रास्त्रिः सप्त सप्ततीनाम् । एभिः सोमेभिः सोमसुद्भिः सोमपा दानाय शुक्रपूतपाः ॥
8.46.e: Who with thrice seven times seventy horses comes to us, invested with the rays of morn,  Through these our Soma-draughts and those who press, to give, drinker of pure bright Soma Juice.

8.46.d: यो म इमं चिदु त्मनामन्दच्चित्रं दावने । अरट्वे अक्षे नहुषे सुकृत्वनि सुकृत्तराय सुक्रतुः ॥
8.46.e: Who hath inclined this glorious one, bounteous himself, to give me gifts.  Borne on firm chariot with the prosperous Nahuṣa, wise, to a man yet more devout.

8.46.d: उचथ्ये३ वपुषि यः स्वराळुत वायो घृतस्नाः । अश्वेषितं रजेषितं शुनेषितं प्राज्म तदिदं नु तत् ॥
8.46.e: Sole Lord in beauty meet for praise, O Vāyu, dropping fatness down,  Hurried along by steeds, by camels, and by hounds, spreads forth thy train: even this it is.

8.46.d: अध प्रियमिषिराय षष्टिं सहस्रासनम् । अश्वानामिन्न वृष्णाम् ॥
8.46.e: So, as a prize dear to the strong, the sixty thousand have I gained,  Bulls that resemble vigorous steeds.

8.46.d: गावो न यूथमुप यन्ति वध्रय उप मा यन्ति वध्रयः ॥
8.46.e: To me come oxen like a herd, yea, unto me the oxen come.

8.46.d: अध यच्चारथे गणे शतमुष्ट्राँ अचिक्रदत् । अध श्वित्नेषु विंशतिं शता ॥
8.46.e: And in the grazing herd he made a hundred camels bleat for me,  And twenty hundred mid the white.

8.46.d: शतं दासे बल्बूथे विप्रस्तरुक्ष आ ददे । ते ते वायविमे जना मदन्तीन्द्रगोपा मदन्ति देवगोपाः ॥
8.46.e: A hundred has the sage received, Dāsa Balbūtha's and Tarukṣa's gifts.  These are thy people, Vāyu, who rejoice with Indra for their guard, rejoice with Gods for guards.

8.46.d: अध स्या योषणा मही प्रतीची वशमश्व्यम् । अधिरुक्मा वि नीयते ॥
8.46.e: And now to Vaśa Aśvya here this stately woman is led forth,  Adorned with ornaments of gold.

8.47.d: महि वो महतामवो वरुण मित्र दाशुषे । यमादित्या अभि द्रुहो रक्षथा नेमघं नशदनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: GREAT help ye give the worshipper, Varuṇa, Mitra, Mighty Ones! No sorrow ever reaches him whom ye, Ādityas, keep from harm. Yours are incomparable aids, and good the succour they afford.

8.47.d: विदा देवा अघानामादित्यासो अपाकृतिम् । पक्षा वयो यथोपरि व्य१स्मे शर्म यच्छतानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: O Gods, Ādityas, well ye know the way to keep all woes afar.  As the birds spread their sheltering wings, spread your protection over us.

8.47.d: व्य१स्मे अधि शर्म तत्पक्षा वयो न यन्तन । विश्वानि विश्ववेदसो वरूथ्या मनामहेऽनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: As the birds spread their sheltering wings let your protection cover us.  We mean all shelter and defence, ye who have all things for your own.

8.47.d: यस्मा अरासत क्षयं जीवातुं च प्रचेतसः । मनोर्विश्वस्य घेदिम आदित्या राय ईशतेऽनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: To whomsoever they, Most Wise, have given a home and means of life,  O'er the whole riches of this man they, the Ādityas, have control.

8.47.d: परि णो वृणजन्नघा दुर्गाणि रथ्यो यथा । स्यामेदिन्द्रस्य शर्मण्यादित्यानामुतावस्यनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: As drivers of the car avoid ill roads, let sorrows pass us by.  May we be under Indra's guard, in the Ādityas’ favouring grace.

8.47.d: परिह्वृतेदना जनो युष्मादत्तस्य वायति । देवा अदभ्रमाश वो यमादित्या अहेतनानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: For verily men sink and faint through loss of wealth which ye have given.  Much hath he gained from you, O Gods, whom ye, Ādityas, have approached.

8.47.d: न तं तिग्मं चन त्यजो न द्रासदभि तं गुरु । यस्मा उ शर्म सप्रथ आदित्यासो अराध्वमनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: On him shall no fierce anger fall, no sore distress shall visit him,  To whom, Ādityas, ye have lent your shelter that extendeth far.

8.47.d: युष्मे देवा अपि ष्मसि युध्यन्त इव वर्मसु । यूयं महो न एनसो यूयमर्भादुरुष्यतानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: Resting in you, O Gods, we are like men who fight in coats of mail.  Ye guard us from each great offence, ye guard us from each lighter fault.

8.47.d: अदितिर्न उरुष्यत्वदितिः शर्म यच्छतु । माता मित्रस्य रेवतोऽर्यम्णो वरुणस्य चानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: May Aditi defend us, may Aditi guard and shelter us,  Mother of wealthy Mitra and of Aryaman and Varuṇa.

8.47.d: यद्देवाः शर्म शरणं यद्भद्रं यदनातुरम् । त्रिधातु यद्वरूथ्यं१ तदस्मासु वि यन्तनानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: The shelter, Gods, that is secure, auspicious, free from malady,  A sure protection, triply strong, even that do ye extend to us.

8.47.d: आदित्या अव हि ख्यताधि कूलादिव स्पशः । सुतीर्थमर्वतो यथानु नो नेषथा सुगमनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: Look down on us, Ādityas, as a guide exploring from the bank.  Lead us to pleasant ways as men lead horses to an easy ford.

8.47.d: नेह भद्रं रक्षस्विने नावयै नोपया उत । गवे च भद्रं धेनवे वीराय च श्रवस्यतेऽनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: Ill be it for the demons' friend to find us or come near to us.  But for the milch-cow be it well, and for the man who strives for fame.

8.47.d: यदाविर्यदपीच्यं१ देवासो अस्ति दुष्कृतम् । त्रिते तद्विश्वमाप्त्य आरे अस्मद्दधातनानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: Each evil deed made manifest, and that which is concealed, O Gods,  The whole thereof remove from us to Trita Āptya far away.

8.47.d: यच्च गोषु दुष्ष्वप्न्यं यच्चास्मे दुहितर्दिवः । त्रिताय तद्विभावर्याप्त्याय परा वहानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: Daughter of Heaven, the dream that bodes evil to us or to our kine,  Remove, O Lady of the Light, to Trita Āptya far away.

8.47.d: निष्कं वा घा कृणवते स्रजं वा दुहितर्दिवः । त्रिते दुष्ष्वप्न्यं सर्वमाप्त्ये परि दद्मस्यनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: Even if, O Child of Heaven, it make a garland or a chain of gold,  The whole bad dream, whate’er it be, to Trita Āptya we consign.

8.47.d: तदन्नाय तदपसे तं भागमुपसेदुषे । त्रिताय च द्विताय चोषो दुष्ष्वप्न्यं वहानेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: To him whose food and work is this, who comes to take his share therein,  To Trita, and to Dvita, Dawn! bear thou the evil dream away.

8.47.d: यथा कलां यथा शफं यथ ऋणं संनयामसि । एवा दुष्ष्वप्न्यं सर्वमाप्त्ये सं नयामस्यनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: As we collect the utmost debt, even the eighth and sixteenth part,  So unto Āptya we transfer together all the evil dream.

8.47.d: अजैष्माद्यासनाम चाभूमानागसो वयम् । उषो यस्माद्दुष्ष्वप्न्यादभैष्माप तदुच्छत्वनेहसो व ऊतयः सुऊतयो व ऊतयः ॥
8.47.e: Now have we conquered and obtained, and from our trespasses are free.  Shine thou away the evil dream, O Dawn, whereof we are afraid. Yours are incomparable aids, and good the succour they afford.

8.48.d: स्वादोरभक्षि वयसः सुमेधाः स्वाध्यो वरिवोवित्तरस्य । विश्वे यं देवा उत मर्त्यासो मधु ब्रुवन्तो अभि संचरन्ति ॥
8.48.e: WISELY have I enjoyed the savoury viand, religious-thoughted, best to find out treasure,  The food to which all Deities and mortals, calling it meath, gather themselves together.

8.48.d: अन्तश्च प्रागा अदितिर्भवास्यवयाता हरसो दैव्यस्य । इन्दविन्द्रस्य सख्यं जुषाणः श्रौष्टीव धुरमनु राय ऋध्याः ॥
8.48.e: Tlou shalt be Aditi as thou hast entered within, appeaser of celestial anger.  Indu, enjoying Indra's friendship, bring us—as a swift steed the car—forward to riches.

8.48.d: अपाम सोमममृता अभूमागन्म ज्योतिरविदाम देवान् । किं नूनमस्मान्कृणवदरातिः किमु धूर्तिरमृत मर्त्यस्य ॥
8.48.e: We have drunk Soma and become immortal; we have attained the light, the Gods discovered.  Now what may foeman's malice do to harm us? What, O Immortal, mortal man's deception?

8.48.d: शं नो भव हृद आ पीत इन्दो पितेव सोम सूनवे सुशेवः । सखेव सख्य उरुशंस धीरः प्र ण आयुर्जीवसे सोम तारीः ॥
8.48.e: Absorbed into the heart, be sweet, O Indu, as a kind father to his son, O Soma,  As a wise Friend to friend: do thou, wide-ruler, O Soma, lengthen out our days for living.

8.48.d: इमे मा पीता यशस उरुष्यवो रथं न गावः समनाह पर्वसु । ते मा रक्षन्तु विस्रसश्चरित्रादुत मा स्रामाद्यवयन्त्विन्दवः ॥
8.48.e: These glorious drops that give me freedom have I drunk. Closely they knit my joints as straps secure a car.  Let them protect my foot from slipping on the way: yea, let the drops I drink preserve me from disease.

8.48.d: अग्निं न मा मथितं सं दिदीपः प्र चक्षय कृणुहि वस्यसो नः । अथा हि ते मद आ सोम मन्ये रेवाँ इव प्र चरा पुष्टिमच्छ ॥
8.48.e: Make me shine bright like fire produced by friction: give us a clearer sight and make us better.  For in carouse I think of thee, O Soma, Shall I, as a rich man, attain to comfort?

8.48.d: इषिरेण ते मनसा सुतस्य भक्षीमहि पित्र्यस्येव रायः । सोम राजन्प्र ण आयूंषि तारीरहानीव सूर्यो वासराणि ॥
8.48.e: May we enjoy with an enlivened spirit the juice thou givest, like ancestral riches.  O Soma, King, prolong thou our existence as Sūrya makes the shining days grow longer.

8.48.d: सोम राजन्मृळया नः स्वस्ति तव स्मसि व्रत्या३स्तस्य विद्धि । अलर्ति दक्ष उत मन्युरिन्दो मा नो अर्यो अनुकामं परा दाः ॥
8.48.e: King Soma, favour us and make us prosper: we are thy devotees; of this be mindful.  Spirit and power are fresh in us, O Indu give us not up unto our foeman's pleasure.

8.48.d: त्वं हि नस्तन्वः सोम गोपा गात्रेगात्रे निषसत्था नृचक्षाः । यत्ते वयं प्रमिनाम व्रतानि स नो मृळ सुषखा देव वस्यः ॥
8.48.e: For thou hast settled in each joint, O Soma, aim of men's eyes and guardian of our bodies.  When we offend against thine holy statutes, as a kind Friend, God, best of all, be gracious.

8.48.d: ऋदूदरेण सख्या सचेय यो मा न रिष्येद्धर्यश्व पीतः । अयं यः सोमो न्यधाय्यस्मे तस्मा इन्द्रं प्रतिरमेम्यायुः ॥
8.48.e: May I be with the Friend whose heart is tender, who, Lord of Bays! when quaffed will never harm me-  This Soma now deposited within me. For this, I pray for longer life to Indra.

8.48.d: अप त्या अस्थुरनिरा अमीवा निरत्रसन्तमिषीचीरभैषुः । आ सोमो अस्माँ अरुहद्विहाया अगन्म यत्र प्रतिरन्त आयुः ॥
8.48.e: Our maladies have lost their strength and vanished: they feared, and passed away into the darkness.  Soma hath risen in us, exceeding mighty, and we are come where men prolong existence.  12, Fathers, that Indu which our hearts have drunken, Immortal in himself, hath entered mortals.  So let us serve this Soma with oblation, and rest securely in his grace and favour.

8.48.d: यो न इन्दुः पितरो हृत्सु पीतोऽमर्त्यो मर्त्याँ आविवेश । तस्मै सोमाय हविषा विधेम मृळीके अस्य सुमतौ स्याम ॥
8.48.e: , Fathers, that Indu which our hearts have drunken, Immortal in himself, hath entered mortals. So let us serve this Soma with oblation, and rest securely in his grace and favour.

8.48.d: त्वं सोम पितृभिः संविदानोऽनु द्यावापृथिवी आ ततन्थ । तस्मै त इन्दो हविषा विधेम वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणाम् ॥
8.48.e: Associate with the Fathers thou, O Soma, hast spread thyself abroad through earth and heaven.  So with oblation let us serve thee, Indu, and so let us become the lords of riches,

8.48.d: त्रातारो देवा अधि वोचता नो मा नो निद्रा ईशत मोत जल्पिः । वयं सोमस्य विश्वह प्रियासः सुवीरासो विदथमा वदेम ॥
8.48.e: Give us your blessing, O ye Gods’ preservers. Never may sleep or idle talk control us.  But evermore may we, as friends of Soma, speak to the synod with brave sons around us.

8.48.d: त्वं नः सोम विश्वतो वयोधास्त्वं स्वर्विदा विशा नृचक्षाः । त्वं न इन्द ऊतिभिः सजोषाः पाहि पश्चातादुत वा पुरस्तात् ॥
8.48.e: On all sides,. Soma, thou art our life-giver: aim of all eyes, light-finder, come within us.  Indu, of one accord with thy protections both from behind and from before preserve us.

8.49.d: अभि प्र वः सुराधसमिन्द्रमर्च यथा विदे । यो जरितृभ्यो मघवा पुरूवसुः सहस्रेणेव शिक्षति ॥
8.49.e: TO you will I sing Indra's praise who gives good gifts as well we know; The praise of Maghavan who, rich in treasure, aids his singers with wealth thousandfold.

8.49.d: शतानीकेव प्र जिगाति धृष्णुया हन्ति वृत्राणि दाशुषे । गिरेरिव प्र रसा अस्य पिन्विरे दत्राणि पुरुभोजसः ॥
8.49.e: As with a hundred hosts, he rushes boldly on, and for the offerer slays his foes. As from a mountain flow the water-brooks, thus flow his gifts who feedeth many a one.

8.49.d: आ त्वा सुतास इन्दवो मदा य इन्द्र गिर्वणः । आपो न वज्रिन्नन्वोक्यं१ सरः पृणन्ति शूर राधसे ॥
8.49.e: The drops effused, the gladdening draughts, O Indra, Lover of the Son As waters seek the lake where they are wont to rest, fill thee, for bounty, Thunderer.

8.49.d: अनेहसं प्रतरणं विवक्षणं मध्वः स्वादिष्ठमीं पिब । आ यथा मन्दसानः किरासि नः प्र क्षुद्रेव त्मना धृषत् ॥
8.49.e: The matchless draught that strengthens and gives eloquence, the sweetest of the meath drink thou, That in thy joy thou mayst scatter thy gifts o'er us, plenteously, even as the dust.

8.49.d: आ नः स्तोममुप द्रवद्धियानो अश्वो न सोतृभिः । यं ते स्वधावन्त्स्वदयन्ति धेनव इन्द्र कण्वेषु रातयः ॥
8.49.e: Come quickly to our laud, urged on by Soma-pressers like a horse- Laud, Godlike Indra, which milch-kine make sweet for thee: with KanVa's sons are gifts for thee.

8.49.d: उग्रं न वीरं नमसोप सेदिम विभूतिमक्षितावसुम् । उद्रीव वज्रिन्नवतो न सिञ्चते क्षरन्तीन्द्र धीतयः ॥
8.49.e: With homage have we sought thee as a Hero, strong, preeminent, with unfailing wealth. O Thunderer, as a plenteous spring pours forth its stream, so, Indra, flow our songs to thee.

8.49.d: यद्ध नूनं यद्वा यज्ञे यद्वा पृथिव्यामधि । अतो नो यज्ञमाशुभिर्महेमत उग्र उग्रेभिरा गहि ॥
8.49.e: If now thou art at sacrifice, or if thou art upon the earth, Come thence, high-thoughted! to our sacrifice with the Swift, come, Mighty with the Mighty Ones.

8.49.d: अजिरासो हरयो ये त आशवो वाता इव प्रसक्षिणः । येभिरपत्यं मनुषः परीयसे येभिर्विश्वं स्वर्दृशे ॥
8.49.e: The active, fleet-foot, tawny Coursers that are thine are swift to victory, like the Wind, Wherewith thou goest round to visit Manus' seed, wherewith all heaven is visible.

8.49.d: एतावतस्त ईमह इन्द्र सुम्नस्य गोमतः । यथा प्रावो मघवन्मेध्यातिथिं यथा नीपातिथिं धने ॥
8.49.e: Indra, from thee so great we crave prosperity in wealth of kine, As, Maghavan, thou favouredst Medhyātithi, and, in the fight, Nipatithi.

8.49.d: यथा कण्वे मघवन्त्रसदस्यवि यथा पक्थे दशव्रजे । यथा गोशर्ये असनोर्ऋजिश्वनीन्द्र गोमद्धिरण्यवत् ॥
8.49.e: As, Maghavan, to KanVa, Trasadasyu, and to Paktha and Dasavraja; As, Indra, to GoSarya and Ṛjiśvan, thou vouchsafedst wealth in kine and gold.

8.50.d: प्र सु श्रुतं सुराधसमर्चा शक्रमभिष्टये । यः सुन्वते स्तुवते काम्यं वसु सहस्रेणेव मंहते ॥
8.50.e: Śakra I praise, to win his aid, far-famed, exceeding bountiful, Who gives, as 'twere in thousands, precious wealth to him who sheds the juice and worships him.

8.50.d: शतानीका हेतयो अस्य दुष्टरा इन्द्रस्य समिषो महीः । गिरिर्न भुज्मा मघवत्सु पिन्वते यदीं सुता अमन्दिषुः ॥
8.50.e: Arrows with hundred points, unconquerable, are this Indra's n-dghty arms in war. He streams on liberal worshippers like a hill with springs, ẉhen juices poured have gladdened him.

8.50.d: यदीं सुतास इन्दवोऽभि प्रियममन्दिषुः । आपो न धायि सवनं म आ वसो दुघा इवोप दाशुषे ॥
8.50.e: What time the flowing Soma-drops have gladdened with their taste the Friend, Like water, gracious Lord! were my libations made, like milch-kine to the worshipper.

8.50.d: अनेहसं वो हवमानमूतये मध्वः क्षरन्ति धीतयः । आ त्वा वसो हवमानास इन्दव उप स्तोत्रेषु दधिरे ॥
8.50.e: To him the peerless, who is calling you to give you aid, forth flow the drops of pleasant meath. The Soloa-drops which call on thee, O gracious Lord, have brought thee to our hymn of praise.

8.50.d: आ नः सोमे स्वध्वर इयानो अत्यो न तोशते । यं ते स्वदावन्त्स्वदन्ति गूर्तयः पौरे छन्दयसे हवम् ॥
8.50.e: He rushes hurrying like a steed to Soma that adorns our rite, Which hymns make sweet to thee, lover of pleasant food. The call to Paura thou dost love.

8.50.d: प्र वीरमुग्रं विविचिं धनस्पृतं विभूतिं राधसो महः । उद्रीव वज्रिन्नवतो वसुत्वना सदा पीपेथ दाशुषे ॥
8.50.e: Praise the strong, grasping Hero, winner of the spoil, ruling supreme oer mighty wealth. Like a full spring, O Thunderer, from thy store hast thou poured on the worshipper evermore.

8.50.d: यद्ध नूनं परावति यद्वा पृथिव्यां दिवि । युजान इन्द्र हरिभिर्महेमत ऋष्व ऋष्वेभिरा गहि ॥
8.50.e: Now whether thou be far away, or in the heavens, or on the earth, O Indra, mighty- thoughted, harnessing thy Bays, come Lofty with the Lofty Ones.

8.50.d: रथिरासो हरयो ये ते अस्रिध ओजो वातस्य पिप्रति । येभिर्नि दस्युं मनुषो निघोषयो येभिः स्वः परीयसे ॥
8.50.e: The Bays who draw thy chariot, Steeds who injure none, surpass the wind's impetuous strength- With whom thou silencest the enemy of man, with whon; thou goest round the sky.

8.50.d: एतावतस्ते वसो विद्याम शूर नव्यसः । यथा प्राव एतशं कृत्व्ये धने यथा वशं दशव्रजे ॥
8.50.e: O gracious Hero, may we learn anew to know thee as thou art: As in decisive fight thou holpest Etaśa, or Vaśa 'gainst Dasavraja,

8.50.d: यथा कण्वे मघवन्मेधे अध्वरे दीर्घनीथे दमूनसि । यथा गोशर्ये असिषासो अद्रिवो मयि गोत्रं हरिश्रियम् ॥
8.50.e: As, Maghavan, to KanVa at the sacred feast, to Dīrghanītha thine home-friend, As to GoSarya thou, Stone-darter, gavest wealth, give me a gold-bright stall of kine.

8.51.d: यथा मनौ सांवरणौ सोममिन्द्रापिबः सुतम् । नीपातिथौ मघवन्मेध्यातिथौ पुष्टिगौ श्रुष्टिगौ सचा ॥
8.51.e: As with Manu Samvarani, Indra, thou drankest Soma juice,  And, Maghavan, with Nipatithi, Medbyatithi, with Pustigu and Srustigu,—

8.51.d: पार्षद्वाणः प्रस्कण्वं समसादयच्छयानं जिव्रिमुद्धितम् । सहस्राण्यसिषासद्गवामृषिस्त्वोतो दस्यवे वृकः ॥
8.51.e: The son of Pṛṣadvāna was Praskaṇva's host, who lay decrepit and forlorn. Aided by thee the Ṛṣi Dasyave-vṛka strove to obtain thousands of kine.

8.51.d: य उक्थेभिर्न विन्धते चिकिद्य ऋषिचोदनः । इन्द्रं तमच्छा वद नव्यस्या मत्यरिष्यन्तं न भोजसे ॥
8.51.e: Lord of swift bounty, he will win e’en with a steed of worthless sort.  This, Indra, must be told of thee who wilt perform heroic deeds.

8.51.d: यस्मा अर्कं सप्तशीर्षाणमानृचुस्त्रिधातुमुत्तमे पदे । स त्वि१मा विश्वा भुवनानि चिक्रददादिज्जनिष्ट पौंस्यम् ॥
8.51.e: He unto whom they sang the seven-headed hymn, three-parted, in the loftiest place,  He sent his thunder down on all these living things, and so displayed heroic might.

8.51.d: यो नो दाता वसूनामिन्द्रं तं हूमहे वयम् । विद्मा ह्यस्य सुमतिं नवीयसीं गमेम गोमति व्रजे ॥
8.51.e: We invocate that Indra who bestoweth precious things on us.  Now do we know his newest favour; may we gain a stable that is full of kine.

8.51.d: यस्मै त्वं वसो दानाय शिक्षसि स रायस्पोषमश्नुते । तं त्वा वयं मघवन्निन्द्र गिर्वणः सुतावन्तो हवामहे ॥
8.51.e: He whom thou aidest, gracious Lord, to give again, obtains great wealth to nourish him.  We with our Soma ready, Lover of the Song! call, Indra Maghavan, on thee.

8.51.d: कदा चन स्तरीरसि नेन्द्र सश्चसि दाशुषे । उपोपेन्नु मघवन्भूय इन्नु ते दानं देवस्य पृच्यते ॥
8.51.e: Ne’er art thou fruitless, Indra ne’er dost thou desert the worshipper  But now, O Maghavan, thy bounty as a God is poured forth ever more and more.

8.51.d: प्र यो ननक्षे अभ्योजसा क्रिविं वधैः शुष्णं निघोषयन् । यदेदस्तम्भीत्प्रथयन्नमूं दिवमादिज्जनिष्ट पार्थिवः ॥
8.51.e: He who hath. overtaken Krvi with his might, and silenced Śuṣṇa with deathbolts,—  When he supported yonder heaven and spread it out, then first the son of earth was born.

8.51.d: यस्यायं विश्व आर्यो दासः शेवधिपा अरिः । तिरश्चिदर्ये रुशमे परीरवि तुभ्येत्सो अज्यते रयिः ॥
8.51.e: Good Lord of wealth is he to whom all Āryas, Dāsas here belong.  Directly unto thee, the pious Ruśama Paviru, is that wealth brought nigh.

8.51.d: तुरण्यवो मधुमन्तं घृतश्चुतं विप्रासो अर्कमानृचुः । अस्मे रयिः पप्रथे वृष्ण्यं शवोऽस्मे सुवानास इन्दवः ॥
8.51.e: In zealous haste the singers have sung forth a song distilling oil and rich in sweets. Riches have spread among us and heroic strength, with us are flowing Soma-drops.

8.52.d: यथा मनौ विवस्वति सोमं शक्रापिबः सुतम् । यथा त्रिते छन्द इन्द्र जुजोषस्यायौ मादयसे सचा ॥
8.52.e: As, Śakra, thou with Manu called Vivasvān drankest Soma juice, As, Indra, thou didst love the hymn by Tṛta's side, so dost thou joy with Āyu now.

8.52.d: पृषध्रे मेध्ये मातरिश्वनीन्द्र सुवाने अमन्दथाः । यथा सोमं दशशिप्रे दशोण्ये स्यूमरश्मावृजूनसि ॥
8.52.e: As thou with Mātariśvan, Medhya, Pṛshadhra, hast cheered thee Indra, with pressed juice, Drunk Soma with Ṛjūnas, Syūmaraśmi, by Daṣoṇya's Daṣaṣipra's side.

8.52.d: य उक्था केवला दधे यः सोमं धृषितापिबत् । यस्मै विष्णुस्त्रीणि पदा विचक्रम उप मित्रस्य धर्मभिः ॥
8.52.e: Tis he who made the lauds his own and boldly drank the Soma juice, He to whom Viṣṇu came striding his three wide steps, as Mitra's statutes ordered it.

8.52.d: यस्य त्वमिन्द्र स्तोमेषु चाकनो वाजे वाजिञ्छतक्रतो । तं त्वा वयं सुदुघामिव गोदुहो जुहूमसि श्रवस्यवः ॥
8.52.e: In whose laud thou didst joy, Indra, at the great deed, O Śatakratu, Mighty One! Seeking renown we call thee as the milkers call the cow who yields abundant milk.

8.52.d: यो नो दाता स नः पिता महाँ उग्र ईशानकृत् । अयामन्नुग्रो मघवा पुरूवसुर्गोरश्वस्य प्र दातु नः ॥
8.52.e: He is our Sire who gives to us, Great, Mighty, ruling as he wills. Unsought, may he the Strong, Rich, Lord of ample wealth, give us of horses and of kine.

8.52.d: यस्मै त्वं वसो दानाय मंहसे स रायस्पोषमिन्वति । वसूयवो वसुपतिं शतक्रतुं स्तोमैरिन्द्रं हवामहे ॥
8.52.e: He to whom thou, Good Lord, givest that he may give increases wealth that nourishes. Eager for wealth we call on Indra, Lord of wealth, on Śatakratu with our lauds.

8.52.d: कदा चन प्र युच्छस्युभे नि पासि जन्मनी । तुरीयादित्य हवनं त इन्द्रियमा तस्थावमृतं दिवि ॥
8.52.e: Never art thou neglectful: thou guardest both races with thy care. The call on Indra, fourth Āditya! is thine own. Amrit is stablished in the heavens.

8.52.d: यस्मै त्वं मघवन्निन्द्र गिर्वणः शिक्षो शिक्षसि दाशुषे । अस्माकं गिर उत सुष्टुतिं वसो कण्ववच्छृणुधी हवम् ॥
8.52.e: The offerer whom thou, Indra, Lover of the Song, liberal Maghavan, favourest,– As at the call of KanVa so, O gracious Lord, hear, thou our songs and eulogy.

8.52.d: अस्तावि मन्म पूर्व्यं ब्रह्मेन्द्राय वोचत । पूर्वीर्ऋतस्य बृहतीरनूषत स्तोतुर्मेधा असृक्षत ॥
8.52.e: Sung is the song of ancient time: to Indra have ye said the prayer. They have sung many a Brhati of sacrifice, poured forth the worshipper's many thoughts.

8.52.d: समिन्द्रो रायो बृहतीरधूनुत सं क्षोणी समु सूर्यम् । सं शुक्रासः शुचयः सं गवाशिरः सोमा इन्द्रममन्दिषुः ॥
8.52.e: Indra hath tossed together mighty stores of wealth, and both the worlds, yea, and the Sun. Pure, brightly-shining, mingled with the milk, the draughts of Soma have made Indra glad.

8.53.d: उपमं त्वा मघोनां ज्येष्ठं च वृषभाणाम् । पूर्भित्तमं मघवन्निन्द्र गोविदमीशानं राय ईमहे ॥
8.53.e: As highest of the Maghavans, preeminent among the Bulls, Best breaker-down of forts, kine-winner, Lord of wealth, we seek thee, Indra Maghavan.

8.53.d: य आयुं कुत्समतिथिग्वमर्दयो वावृधानो दिवेदिवे । तं त्वा वयं हर्यश्वं शतक्रतुं वाजयन्तो हवामहे ॥
8.53.e: Thou who subduedst Āyu, Kutsa, Atithigva, waxing daily in thy might, As such, rousing thy power, we invocate thee now, thee Śatakratu, Lord of Bays.

8.53.d: आ नो विश्वेषां रसं मध्वः सिञ्चन्त्वद्रयः । ये परावति सुन्विरे जनेष्वा ये अर्वावतीन्दवः ॥
8.53.e: The pressing-stones shall pour for us the essence of the meath of all, Drops that have been pressed out afar among the folk, and those that have been pressed near us.

8.53.d: विश्वा द्वेषांसि जहि चाव चा कृधि विश्वे सन्वन्त्वा वसु । शीष्टेषु चित्ते मदिरासो अंशवो यत्रा सोमस्य तृम्पसि ॥
8.53.e: Repel all enmities and keep them far away: let all win treasure for their own. Even among Ṣishṭas are the stalks that make thee glad, where thou with Soma satest thee.

8.53.d: इन्द्र नेदीय एदिहि मितमेधाभिरूतिभिः । आ शंतम शंतमाभिरभिष्टिभिरा स्वापे स्वापिभिः ॥
8.53.e: Come, Indra, very near to us with aids of firmly-based resolve; Come, most auspicious, with thy most auspicious help, good Kinsman, with good kinsmen, come!

8.53.d: आजितुरं सत्पतिं विश्वचर्षणिं कृधि प्रजास्वाभगम् । प्र सू तिरा शचीभिर्ये त उक्थिनः क्रतुं पुनत आनुषक् ॥
8.53.e: Bless thou with progeny the chief of men, the lord of heroes, victor in the fray. Aid with thy powers the men who sing thee lauds and keep their spirits ever pure and bright.

8.53.d: यस्ते साधिष्ठोऽवसे ते स्याम भरेषु ते । वयं होत्राभिरुत देवहूतिभिः ससवांसो मनामहे ॥
8.53.e: May we be such in battle as are surest to obtain thy grace: With holy offerings and invocations of the Gods, we mean, that we may win the spoil.

8.53.d: अहं हि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म वाजयुराजिं यामि सदोतिभिः । त्वामिदेव तममे समश्वयुर्गव्युरग्रे मथीनाम् ॥
8.53.e: Thine, Lord of Bays, am I. Prayer longeth for the spoil. Still with thy help I seek the fight. So, at the raiders' head, I, craving steeds and kine, unite myself with thee alone.

8.54.d: एतत्त इन्द्र वीर्यं गीर्भिर्गृणन्ति कारवः । ते स्तोभन्त ऊर्जमावन्घृतश्चुतं पौरासो नक्षन्धीतिभिः ॥
8.54.e: INDRA, the poets with their hymns extol this hero might of thine: They strengthened, loud in song, thy power that droppeth oil. With hymns the Pauras came to thee.

8.54.d: नक्षन्त इन्द्रमवसे सुकृत्यया येषां सुतेषु मन्दसे । यथा संवर्ते अमदो यथा कृश एवास्मे इन्द्र मत्स्व ॥
8.54.e: Through piety they came to Indra for his aid, they whose libations give theejoy. As thou with, Krsa and Samvarta hast rejoiced, so, Indra, be thou glad with us.

8.54.d: आ नो विश्वे सजोषसो देवासो गन्तनोप नः । वसवो रुद्रा अवसे न आ गमञ्छृण्वन्तु मरुतो हवम् ॥
8.54.e: Agreeing in your spirit, all ye Deities, come nigh to us. Vasus and Rudras shall come near to give us aid, and Maruts listen to our call.

8.54.d: पूषा विष्णुर्हवनं मे सरस्वत्यवन्तु सप्त सिन्धवः । आपो वातः पर्वतासो वनस्पतिः शृणोतु पृथिवी हवम् ॥
8.54.e: May Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, and Sarasvatī befriend, and the Seven Streams, this call of mine: May Waters, Wind, the Mountains, and the Forest-Lord, and Earth give ear unto my cry.

8.54.d: यदिन्द्र राधो अस्ति ते माघोनं मघवत्तम । तेन नो बोधि सधमाद्यो वृधे भगो दानाय वृत्रहन् ॥
8.54.e: Indra, with thine own bounteous gift, most liberal of the Mighty Ones, Be our boon benefactor, Vṛtra-slayer, be our feast-companion for our weal.

8.54.d: आजिपते नृपते त्वमिद्धि नो वाज आ वक्षि सुक्रतो । वीती होत्राभिरुत देववीतिभिः ससवांसो वि शृण्विरे ॥
8.54.e: Leader of heroes, Lord of battle, lead thou us to combat, thou Most Sapient One. High fame is theirs who win by invocations, feasts and entertainment of the Gods.

8.54.d: सन्ति ह्य१र्य आशिष इन्द्र आयुर्जनानाम् । अस्मान्नक्षस्व मघवन्नुपावसे धुक्षस्व पिप्युषीमिषम् ॥
8.54.e: Our hopes rest on the Faithful One: In Indra is the people's life. O Maghavan, come nigh that thou mayst give us aid: make plenteous food stream forth for us.

8.54.d: वयं त इन्द्र स्तोमेभिर्विधेम त्वमस्माकं शतक्रतो । महि स्थूरं शशयं राधो अह्रयं प्रस्कण्वाय नि तोशय ॥
8.54.e: Thee would we worship, Indra, with our songs of praise: O Śatakratu, be thou ours. Pour down upon Praskaṇva bounty vast and firm, exuberant, that shall never fail.

8.55.d: भूरीदिन्द्रस्य वीर्यं१ व्यख्यमभ्यायति । राधस्ते दस्यवे वृक ॥
8.55.e: GREAT, verily, is Indra's might. I have beheld, and hither comes Thy bounty, Dasyave-vṛka!

8.55.d: शतं श्वेतास उक्षणो दिवि तारो न रोचन्ते । मह्ना दिवं न तस्तभुः ॥
8.55.e: A hundred oxen white of hue are shining like the stars in heaven, So tall, they seem to prop the sky.

8.55.d: शतं वेणूञ्छतं शुनः शतं चर्माणि म्लातानि । शतं मे बल्बजस्तुका अरुषीणां चतुःशतम् ॥
8.55.e: Bamboos a hundred, a hundred dogs, a hundred skins of beasts well-tanned, A hundred tufts of Balbaja, four hundred red-hued mares are mine.

8.55.d: सुदेवाः स्थ काण्वायना वयोवयो विचरन्तः । अश्वासो न चङ्क्रमत ॥
8.55.e: Blest by the Gods, Kinvayanas! be ye who spread through life on life: Like horses have ye stridden forth.

8.55.d: आदित्साप्तस्य चर्किरन्नानूनस्य महि श्रवः । श्यावीरतिध्वसन्पथश्चक्षुषा चन संनशे ॥
8.55.e: Then men extolled the team of seven not yet full-grown, its fame is great. The dark mares rushed along the paths, so that no eye could follow them.

8.56.d: प्रति ते दस्यवे वृक राधो अदर्श्यह्रयम् । द्यौर्न प्रथिना शवः ॥
8.56.e: THY bounty, Dasyave-vṛka, exhaustless hath displayed itself: Its fulness is as broad as heaven.

8.56.d: दश मह्यं पौतक्रतः सहस्रा दस्यवे वृकः । नित्याद्रायो अमंहत ॥
8.56.e: Ten thousand Dasyave-vṛka, the son of Pūtakratu, hath From his own wealth bestowed on me.

8.56.d: शतं मे गर्दभानां शतमूर्णावतीनाम् । शतं दासाँ अति स्रजः ॥
8.56.e: A hundred asses hath he given, a hundred head of fleecy sheep, A hundred slaves, and wreaths besides.

8.56.d: तत्रो अपि प्राणीयत पूतक्रतायै व्यक्ता । अश्वानामिन्न यूथ्याम् ॥
8.56.e: There also was a mare led forth, picked out for Putakrata's sake, Not of the horses of the herd.

8.56.d: अचेत्यग्निश्चिकितुर्हव्यवाट् स सुमद्रथः । अग्निः शुक्रेण शोचिषा बृहत्सूरो अरोचत दिवि सूर्यो अरोचत ॥
8.56.e: Observant Agni hath appeared, oblation-bearer with his car. Agni with his resplendent flame hath shone on high as shines the Sun, hath shone like Sūrya in the heavens.

8.57.d: युवं देवा क्रतुना पूर्व्येण युक्ता रथेन तविषं यजत्रा । आगच्छतं नासत्या शचीभिरिदं तृतीयं सवनं पिबाथः ॥
8.57.e: ENDOWED, O Gods, with your primeval wisdom, come quickly with your chariot, O ye Holy. Come with your mighty powers, O ye Nāsatyas; come hither, drink ye this the third libation.

8.57.d: युवां देवास्त्रय एकादशासः सत्याः सत्यस्य ददृशे पुरस्तात् । अस्माकं यज्ञं सवनं जुषाणा पातं सोममश्विना दीद्यग्नी ॥
8.57.e: The truthful Deities, the Three-and-Thirty, saw you approach before the Ever-Truthful. Accepting this our worship and libation, O Aśvins bright with fire, drink ye the Soma.

8.57.d: पनाय्यं तदश्विना कृतं वां वृषभो दिवो रजसः पृथिव्याः । सहस्रं शंसा उत ये गविष्टौ सर्वाँ इत्ताँ उप याता पिबध्यै ॥
8.57.e: Aśvins, that work of yours deserves our wonder,– the Bull of heaven and earth and air's mid region; Yea, and your thousand promises in battle, -to all of these come near and drink beside us.

8.57.d: अयं वां भागो निहितो यजत्रेमा गिरो नासत्योप यातम् । पिबतं सोमं मधुमन्तमस्मे प्र दाश्वांसमवतं शचीभिः ॥
8.57.e: Here is your portion laid for you, ye Holy: come to these songs of ours, O ye Nāsatyas. Drink among us the Soma full of sweetness, and with your powers assist the man who worships.

8.58.d: यमृत्विजो बहुधा कल्पयन्तः सचेतसो यज्ञमिमं वहन्ति । यो अनूचानो ब्राह्मणो युक्त आसीत्का स्वित्तत्र यजमानस्य संवित् ॥
8.58.e: HE whom the priests in sundry ways arranging the sacrifice, of one accord, bring hither, Who was appointed as a learned Brahman, -what is the sacrificer's knowledge of him?

8.58.d: एक एवाग्निर्बहुधा समिद्ध एकः सूर्यो विश्वमनु प्रभूतः । एकैवोषाः सर्वमिदं वि भात्येकं वा इदं वि बभूव सर्वम् ॥
8.58.e: Kindled in many a spot, still One is Agni; Sūrya is One though high o'er all he shineth. Illumining this All, still One is Uṣas. That which is One hath into All developed.

8.58.d: ज्योतिष्मन्तं केतुमन्तं त्रिचक्रं सुखं रथं सुषदं भूरिवारम् । चित्रामघा यस्य योगेऽधिजज्ञे तं वां हुवे अति रिक्तं पिबध्यै ॥
8.58.e: The chariot bright and radiant, treasure-laden, three-wheeled, with easy seat, and lightly rolling, Which She of Wondrous Wealth was born to harness,– this car of yours I call. Drink what remaineth.

8.59.d: इमानि वां भागधेयानि सिस्रत इन्द्रावरुणा प्र महे सुतेषु वाम् । यज्ञेयज्ञे ह सवना भुरण्यथो यत्सुन्वते यजमानाय शिक्षथः ॥
8.59.e: IN offerings poured to you, O Indra-VARUNA, these shares of yours stream forth to glorify your state. Ye haste to the libations at each sacrifice ẉhen ye assist the worshipper who sheds the juice.

8.59.d: निष्षिध्वरीरोषधीराप आस्तामिन्द्रावरुणा महिमानमाशत । या सिस्रतू रजसः पारे अध्वनो ययोः शत्रुर्नकिरादेव ओहते ॥
8.59.e: The waters and the plants, O Indra-VARUNA, had efficacious vigour, and attained to might: Ye who have gone beyond the path of middle air,– no godless man is worthy to be called your foe.

8.59.d: सत्यं तदिन्द्रावरुणा कृशस्य वां मध्व ऊर्मिं दुहते सप्त वाणीः । ताभिर्दाश्वांसमवतं शुभस्पती यो वामदब्धो अभि पाति चित्तिभिः ॥
8.59.e: True is your Krsa's word, Indra and VARUNA: The seven holy voices pour a wave of meath. For their sake, Lords of splendour! aid the pious man who, unbewildered, keeps you ever in his thoughts.

8.59.d: घृतप्रुषः सौम्या जीरदानवः सप्त स्वसारः सदन ऋतस्य । या ह वामिन्द्रावरुणा घृतश्चुतस्ताभिर्धत्तं यजमानाय शिक्षतम् ॥
8.59.e: Dropping oil, sweet with Soma, pouring forth their stream, are the Seven Sisters in the seat of sacrifice. These, dropping oil, are yours, O Indra-VARUNA: with these enrich with gifts and help the worshipper.

8.59.d: अवोचाम महते सौभगाय सत्यं त्वेषाभ्यां महिमानमिन्द्रियम् । अस्मान्त्स्विन्द्रावरुणा घृतश्चुतस्त्रिभिः साप्तेभिरवतं शुभस्पती ॥
8.59.e: To our great happiness have we ascribed to these Two Bright Ones truthfulness, great strength, and majesty. O Lords of splendour, aid us through the Three-times-Seven, as we pour holy oil, O Indra-VARUNA.

8.59.d: इन्द्रावरुणा यदृषिभ्यो मनीषां वाचो मतिं श्रुतमदत्तमग्रे । यानि स्थानान्यसृजन्त धीरा यज्ञं तन्वानास्तपसाभ्यपश्यम् ॥
8.59.e: What ye in time of old Indra and VARUNA, gave Ṛṣis revelation, thought, and power of song, And places which the wise made, weaving sacrifice,– these through my spirit's fervid glow have I beheld.,

8.59.d: इन्द्रावरुणा सौमनसमदृप्तं रायस्पोषं यजमानेषु धत्तम् । प्रजां पुष्टिं भूतिमस्मासु धत्तं दीर्घायुत्वाय प्र तिरतं न आयुः ॥
8.59.e: O Indra-VARUNA, grant to the worshippers cheerfulness void of pride, and wealth to nourish them. Vouchsafe us food, prosperity, and progeny, and lengthen out our days that we may see long life.

8.60.d: अग्न आ याह्यग्निभिर्होतारं त्वा वृणीमहे । आ त्वामनक्तु प्रयता हविष्मती यजिष्ठं बर्हिरासदे ॥
8.60.e: AGNI, come hither with thy fires; we choose thee as Invoking Priest.  Let the extended ladle full of oil balm thee, best Priest, to sit on sacred grass.

8.60.d: अच्छा हि त्वा सहसः सूनो अङ्गिरः स्रुचश्चरन्त्यध्वरे । ऊर्जो नपातं घृतकेशमीमहेऽग्निं यज्ञेषु पूर्व्यम् ॥
8.60.e: For unto thee, O Aṅgiras, O Son of Strength, move ladles in the sacrifice.  To Agni, Child of Force, whose locks drop oil, we seek, foremost in sacrificial rites.

8.60.d: अग्ने कविर्वेधा असि होता पावक यक्ष्यः । मन्द्रो यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्यो विप्रेभिः शुक्र मन्मभिः ॥
8.60.e: Agni, thou art Disposer, Sage, Herald, bright God! and worshipful,  Best offerer, cheerful, to be praised in holy rites, pure Lord! by singers with their hymns.

8.60.d: अद्रोघमा वहोशतो यविष्ठ्य देवाँ अजस्र वीतये । अभि प्रयांसि सुधिता वसो गहि मन्दस्व धीतिभिर्हितः ॥
8.60.e: Most Youthful and Eternal, bring the longing Gods to me, the guileless, for the feast.  Come, Vasu, to the banquet that is well-prepared: rejoice thee, gracious, with our songs.

8.60.d: त्वमित्सप्रथा अस्यग्ने त्रातर्ऋतस्कविः । त्वां विप्रासः समिधान दीदिव आ विवासन्ति वेधसः ॥
8.60.e: Famed art thou, Agni, far and wide, Preserver, righteous, and a Sage.  The holy singers, O refulgent kindled God! arrangers, call on thee to come.

8.60.d: शोचा शोचिष्ठ दीदिहि विशे मयो रास्व स्तोत्रे महाँ असि । देवानां शर्मन्मम सन्तु सूरयः शत्रूषाहः स्वग्नयः ॥
8.60.e: Shine, Most Resplendent! blaze, send bliss unto the folk, and to thy worshipper  Great art thou.  So may my princes, with good fires, subduing foes, rest in the keeping of the Gods.

8.60.d: यथा चिद्वृद्धमतसमग्ने संजूर्वसि क्षमि । एवा दह मित्रमहो यो अस्मध्रुग्दुर्मन्मा कश्च वेनति ॥
8.60.e: O Agni, as thou burnest down to earth even high-grown underwood,  So, bright as Mitra is, burn him who injures us, him who plots ill against thy friend.

8.60.d: मा नो मर्ताय रिपवे रक्षस्विने माघशंसाय रीरधः । अस्रेधद्भिस्तरणिभिर्यविष्ठ्य शिवेभिः पाहि पायुभिः ॥
8.60.e: Give us not as a prey to mortal enemy, nor to the wicked friend of fiends.  With conquering guards, auspicious, unassailable, protect us, O Most Youthful God.

8.60.d: पाहि नो अग्न एकया पाह्यु१त द्वितीयया । पाहि गीर्भिस्तिसृभिरूर्जां पते पाहि चतसृभिर्वसो ॥
8.60.e: Protect us, Agni, through the first, protect us through the second hymn,  Protect us through three hymns, O Lord of Power and Might, through four hymns, Vasu, guard thou us.

8.60.d: पाहि विश्वस्माद्रक्षसो अराव्णः प्र स्म वाजेषु नोऽव । त्वामिद्धि नेदिष्ठं देवतातय आपिं नक्षामहे वृधे ॥
8.60.e: Preserve us from each fiend who brings the Gods no gift, preserve thou us in deeds of strength:  For we possess in thee the nearest Friend of all, for service of the Gods and weal.

8.60.d: आ नो अग्ने वयोवृधं रयिं पावक शंस्यम् । रास्वा च न उपमाते पुरुस्पृहं सुनीती स्वयशस्तरम् ॥
8.60.e: O Holy Agni, give us wealth renowned with men and strengthening life. Bestow on us, O Helper, that which many crave, more glorious still by righteousness;

8.60.d: येन वंसाम पृतनासु शर्धतस्तरन्तो अर्य आदिशः । स त्वं नो वर्ध प्रयसा शचीवसो जिन्वा धियो वसुविदः ॥
8.60.e: Wherewith we may o’ercome our rivals in the war, o’erpowering the foe’s designs. So wax thou by our food, O Excellent in strength. Quicken our thoughts that find out wealth.

8.60.d: शिशानो वृषभो यथाग्निः शृङ्गे दविध्वत् । तिग्मा अस्य हनवो न प्रतिधृषे सुजम्भः सहसो यहुः ॥
8.60.e: Agni is even as a bull who whets and brandishes his horns. Well-sharpened are his jaws which may not be withstood: the Child of Strength hath powerful teeth.

8.60.d: नहि ते अग्ने वृषभ प्रतिधृषे जम्भासो यद्वितिष्ठसे । स त्वं नो होतः सुहुतं हविष्कृधि वंस्वा नो वार्या पुरु ॥
8.60.e: Not to be stayed, O Bull, O Agni, are thy teeth ẉhen thou art spreading far and wide. Make our oblations duly offered up, O Priest, and give us store of precious things.

8.60.d: शेषे वनेषु मात्रोः सं त्वा मर्तास इन्धते । अतन्द्रो हव्या वहसि हविष्कृत आदिद्देवेषु राजसि ॥
8.60.e: Thou liest in the wood: from both thy Mothers mortals kindle thee. Unweariedly thou bearest up the offerer’s gifts, then shinest bright among the Gods.

8.60.d: सप्त होतारस्तमिदीळते त्वाग्ने सुत्यजमह्रयम् । भिनत्स्यद्रिं तपसा वि शोचिषा प्राग्ने तिष्ठ जनाँ अति ॥
8.60.e: And so the seven priests, O Agni, worship thee, Free-giver, Everlasting One. Thou cleavest through the rock with heat and fervent glow. Agni, rise up above the men.

8.60.d: अग्निमग्निं वो अध्रिगुं हुवेम वृक्तबर्हिषः । अग्निं हितप्रयसः शश्वतीष्वा होतारं चर्षणीनाम् ॥
8.60.e: For you let us whose grass is trimmed call Agni, Agni, restless God. Let us whose food is offered call to all the tribes Agni the Invoking Priest of men.

8.60.d: केतेन शर्मन्त्सचते सुषामण्यग्ने तुभ्यं चिकित्वना । इषण्यया नः पुरुरूपमा भर वाजं नेदिष्ठमूतये ॥
8.60.e: Agni, with noble psalm that tells his wish he dwells, thinking on thee who guardest him. Speedily bring us strength of many varied sorts to be most near to succour us.

8.60.d: अग्ने जरितर्विश्पतिस्तेपानो देव रक्षसः । अप्रोषिवान्गृहपतिर्महाँ असि दिवस्पायुर्दुरोणयुः ॥
8.60.e: Agni, Praise-singer! Lord of men, God! burner-up of Rakshasas, Mighty art thou, the ever-present Household-Lord, Home-friend and Guardian from the sky.

8.60.d: मा नो रक्ष आ वेशीदाघृणीवसो मा यातुर्यातुमावताम् । परोगव्यूत्यनिरामप क्षुधमग्ने सेध रक्षस्विनः ॥
8.60.e: Let no fiend come among us, O thou rich in light, no spell of those who deal in spells. To distant pastures drive faint hunger: far away, O Agni, chase the demons’ friends.

8.61.d: उभयं शृणवच्च न इन्द्रो अर्वागिदं वचः । सत्राच्या मघवा सोमपीतये धिया शविष्ठ आ गमत् ॥
8.61.e: BOTH boons,—may Indra, hitherward turned, listen to this prayer of ours,  And mightiest Maghavan with thought inclined to us come near to drink the Soma juice.

8.61.d: तं हि स्वराजं वृषभं तमोजसे धिषणे निष्टतक्षतुः । उतोपमानां प्रथमो नि षीदसि सोमकामं हि ते मनः ॥
8.61.e: For him, strong, independent Ruler, Heaven and Earth have fashioned forth for power and might.  Thou seatest thee as first among thy peers in place, for thy soul longs for Soma juice.

8.61.d: आ वृषस्व पुरूवसो सुतस्येन्द्रान्धसः । विद्मा हि त्वा हरिवः पृत्सु सासहिमधृष्टं चिद्दधृष्वणिम् ॥
8.61.e: Fill thyself full, O Lord of wealth, O Indra, with the juice we shed.  We know thee, Lord of Bay Steeds victor in the fight, vanquishing e’en the invincible.

8.61.d: अप्रामिसत्य मघवन्तथेदसदिन्द्र क्रत्वा यथा वशः । सनेम वाजं तव शिप्रिन्नवसा मक्षू चिद्यन्तो अद्रिवः ॥
8.61.e: Changeless in truth, O Maghavan Indra, let it be as thou in wisdom willest it.  May we, O fair of check, win booty with thine aid, O Thunderer, swiftly seeking it.

8.61.d: शग्ध्यू३ षु शचीपत इन्द्र विश्वाभिरूतिभिः । भगं न हि त्वा यशसं वसुविदमनु शूर चरामसि ॥
8.61.e: Indra, with all thy saving helps give us assistance, Lord of power.  For after thee we follow even as glorious bliss, thee, Hero, finder-out of wealth.

8.61.d: पौरो अश्वस्य पुरुकृद्गवामस्युत्सो देव हिरण्ययः । नकिर्हि दानं परिमर्धिषत्त्वे यद्यद्यामि तदा भर ॥
8.61.e: Increaser of our steeds and multiplying kine, a golden well, O God, art thou,  For no one may impair the gifts laid up in thee. Bring me whatever thing I ask.

8.61.d: त्वं ह्येहि चेरवे विदा भगं वसुत्तये । उद्वावृषस्व मघवन्गविष्टय उदिन्द्राश्वमिष्टये ॥
8.61.e: For thou,—come to the worshipper!—wilt find great wealth to make us rich.  Fill thyself full, O Maghavan, for gain of kine, full, Indra, for the gain of steeds.

8.61.d: त्वं पुरू सहस्राणि शतानि च यूथा दानाय मंहसे । आ पुरंदरं चकृम विप्रवचस इन्द्रं गायन्तोऽवसे ॥
8.61.e: Thou as thy gift bestowest many hundred herds, yea, many thousands dost thou give.  With singers' hymns have we brought the Fort-render near, singing to Indra for his grace.

8.61.d: अविप्रो वा यदविधद्विप्रो वेन्द्र ते वचः । स प्र ममन्दत्त्वाया शतक्रतो प्राचामन्यो अहंसन ॥
8.61.e: Whether the simple or the sage, Indra, have offered praise to thee,  He Śatakratu! by his love hath gladdened thee, ambitious! ever pressing on!

8.61.d: उग्रबाहुर्म्रक्षकृत्वा पुरंदरो यदि मे शृणवद्धवम् । वसूयवो वसुपतिं शतक्रतुं स्तोमैरिन्द्रं हवामहे ॥
8.61.e: If he the Strong of arm, the breaker-down of forts, the great Destroyer, hear my call,  We, seeking riches cry to Indra, Lord of wealth, to Śatakratu with our lauds.

8.61.d: न पापासो मनामहे नारायासो न जळ्हवः । यदिन्न्विन्द्रं वृषणं सचा सुते सखायं कृणवामहै ॥
8.61.e: We count not then as sinners, nor as niggardly or foolish men, When with the Soma juice which we have shed we make Indra, the Mighty One, our Friend.

8.61.d: उग्रं युयुज्म पृतनासु सासहिमृणकातिमदाभ्यम् । वेदा भृमं चित्सनिता रथीतमो वाजिनं यमिदू नशत् ॥
8.61.e: Him have we yoked in fight, the powerful Conqueror, debt-claimer, not to be deceived. Best charioteer, the Victor marks each fault, he knows the strong to whom he will come near.

8.61.d: यत इन्द्र भयामहे ततो नो अभयं कृधि । मघवञ्छग्धि तव तन्न ऊतिभिर्वि द्विषो वि मृधो जहि ॥
8.61.e: Indra, give us security from that whereof we are afraid. Help us, O Maghavan, let thy succour give us this: drive away foes and enemies.

8.61.d: त्वं हि राधस्पते राधसो महः क्षयस्यासि विधतः । तं त्वा वयं मघवन्निन्द्र गिर्वणः सुतावन्तो हवामहे ॥
8.61.e: For thou, O liberal Lord of bounty, strengthenest his ample home who worships thee. So Indra, Maghavan, thou Lover of the Song, we with pressed Soma call on thee.

8.61.d: इन्द्रः स्पळुत वृत्रहा परस्पा नो वरेण्यः । स नो रक्षिषच्चरमं स मध्यमं स पश्चात्पातु नः पुरः ॥
8.61.e: Indra is Vṛtra-slayer, guard, our best defender from the foe. May he preserve our last and middlemost, and keep watch from behind us and before.

8.61.d: त्वं नः पश्चादधरादुत्तरात्पुर इन्द्र नि पाहि विश्वतः । आरे अस्मत्कृणुहि दैव्यं भयमारे हेतीरदेवीः ॥
8.61.e: Defend us from behind, below, above, in front, on all sides, Indra, shield us well. Keep far away from us the terror seat from heaven: keep impious weapons far away.

8.61.d: अद्याद्या श्वःश्व इन्द्र त्रास्व परे च नः । विश्वा च नो जरितॄन्त्सत्पते अहा दिवा नक्तं च रक्षिषः ॥
8.61.e: Protect us, Indra, each to-day, each morrow, and each following day. Our singers, through all days, shalt thou, Lord of the brave, keep safely both by day and night.

8.61.d: प्रभङ्गी शूरो मघवा तुवीमघः सम्मिश्लो विर्याय कम् । उभा ते बाहू वृषणा शतक्रतो नि या वज्रं मिमिक्षतुः ॥
8.61.e: A crushing Warrior, passing rich is Maghavan, endowed with all heroic might. Thine arms, O Śatakratu, are exceeding strong, arms which have grasped the thunderbolt.

8.62.d: प्रो अस्मा उपस्तुतिं भरता यज्जुजोषति । उक्थैरिन्द्रस्य माहिनं वयो वर्धन्ति सोमिनो भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: OFFER ye up as praise to him that wherein Indra takes delight.  The Soma-bringers magnify Indra's great energy with hymns. Good are the gifts that Indra gives.

8.62.d: अयुजो असमो नृभिरेकः कृष्टीरयास्यः । पूर्वीरति प्र वावृधे विश्वा जातान्योजसा भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: Sole among chiefs, companionless, impetuous, and peerless, he  Hath waxen great o’er many folk, yea., over all things born, in might.

8.62.d: अहितेन चिदर्वता जीरदानुः सिषासति । प्रवाच्यमिन्द्र तत्तव वीर्याणि करिष्यतो भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: Call hither with thy newest song Indra who lacks not hymns of praise,  Him who observes and knows, inspirer of the sage, him who seems eager to enjoy.

8.62.d: आ याहि कृणवाम त इन्द्र ब्रह्माणि वर्धना । येभिः शविष्ठ चाकनो भद्रमिह श्रवस्यते भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: Come to us hither: let us pay devotions that enhance thy might,  For which, Most Potent! thou wouldst fain bless the man here who strives for fame.

8.62.d: धृषतश्चिद्धृषन्मनः कृणोषीन्द्र यत्त्वम् । तीव्रैः सोमैः सपर्यतो नमोभिः प्रतिभूषतो भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: For thou, O Indra, makest yet more bold the spirit of the bold  Who with strong Soma serveth thee, still ready with his reverent prayers.

8.62.d: अव चष्ट ऋचीषमोऽवताँ इव मानुषः । जुष्ट्वी दक्षस्य सोमिनः सखायं कृणुते युजं भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: Worthy of song, he looketh down as a man looketh into wells.  Pleased with the Soma-bringer's skill he maketh him his mate and friend.

8.62.d: विश्वे त इन्द्र वीर्यं देवा अनु क्रतुं ददुः । भुवो विश्वस्य गोपतिः पुरुष्टुत भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: In strength and wisdom all the Gods, Indra, have yielded unto thee.  Be thou the Guard of all, O thou whom many praise.

8.62.d: गृणे तदिन्द्र ते शव उपमं देवतातये । यद्धंसि वृत्रमोजसा शचीपते भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: Praised, Indra, is this might of thine, best for the service of the Gods,  That thou with power dost slay Vṛtra, O Lord of Strength.

8.62.d: समनेव वपुष्यतः कृणवन्मानुषा युगा । विदे तदिन्द्रश्चेतनमध श्रुतो भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: He makes the races of mankind like synods of the Beauteous One.  Indra knows this his manifest deed, and is renowned.

8.62.d: उज्जातमिन्द्र ते शव उत्त्वामुत्तव क्रतुम् । भूरिगो भूरि वावृधुर्मघवन्तव शर्मणि भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: Thy might, O Indra, at its birth, thee also, and thy mental power,  In thy care, Maghavan rich in kine! they have increased exceedingly.

8.62.d: अहं च त्वं च वृत्रहन्त्सं युज्याव सनिभ्य आ । अरातीवा चिदद्रिवोऽनु नौ शूर मंसते भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: O Vṛtra-slayer, thou and I will both combine for winning spoil. Even malignity will consent, O Bolt-armed Hero, unto us.

8.62.d: सत्यमिद्वा उ तं वयमिन्द्रं स्तवाम नानृतम् । महाँ असुन्वतो वधो भूरि ज्योतींषि सुन्वतो भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयः ॥
8.62.e: Let us extol this Indra as truthful and never as untrue. Dire is his death who pours no gifts: great light hath he who offers them. Good are the gifts that Indra gives.

8.63.d: स पूर्व्यो महानां वेनः क्रतुभिरानजे । यस्य द्वारा मनुष्पिता देवेषु धिय आनजे ॥
8.63.e: WITH powers of Mighty Ones hath he, Ancient, Beloved, been equipped,  Through whom the Father Manu made prayers efficacious with the Gods.

8.63.d: दिवो मानं नोत्सदन्त्सोमपृष्ठासो अद्रयः । उक्था ब्रह्म च शंस्या ॥
8.63.e: Him, Maker of the sky, let stones wet with the Soma ne’er forsake,  Nor hymns and prayer that must be said.

8.63.d: स विद्वाँ अङ्गिरोभ्य इन्द्रो गा अवृणोदप । स्तुषे तदस्य पौंस्यम् ॥
8.63.e: Indra who knew full well disclosed the kine to the Aṅgirases.  This his great deed must be extolled.

8.63.d: स प्रत्नथा कविवृध इन्द्रो वाकस्य वक्षणिः । शिवो अर्कस्य होमन्यस्मत्रा गन्त्ववसे ॥
8.63.e: Indra, promoter of the song, the sage's Strengthener as of old,  Shall come to bless and succour us at presentation of this laud.

8.63.d: आदू नु ते अनु क्रतुं स्वाहा वरस्य यज्यवः । श्वात्रमर्का अनूषतेन्द्र गोत्रस्य दावने ॥
8.63.e: Now after their desire's intent the pious singers with the cry  Of Hail! have sung loud hymns to thee, Indra, to gain a stall of kine.

8.63.d: इन्द्रे विश्वानि वीर्या कृतानि कर्त्वानि च । यमर्का अध्वरं विदुः ॥
8.63.e: With Indra rest all deeds of might, deeds done and yet to be performed,  Whom singers know devoid of guile.

8.63.d: यत्पाञ्चजन्यया विशेन्द्रे घोषा असृक्षत । अस्तृणाद्बर्हणा विपो३ऽर्यो मानस्य स क्षयः ॥
8.63.e: When the Five Tribes with all their men to Indra have sent out their voice,  And when the priest hath strewn much grass, this is the Friend's own dwelling-place.

8.63.d: इयमु ते अनुष्टुतिश्चकृषे तानि पौंस्या । प्रावश्चक्रस्य वर्तनिम् ॥
8.63.e: This praise is verily thine own: thou hast performed these manly deeds,  And sped the wheel upon its way.

8.63.d: अस्य वृष्णो व्योदन उरु क्रमिष्ट जीवसे । यवं न पश्व आ ददे ॥
8.63.e: At the o’erflowing of this Steer, boldly he strode for life, and took  Soma as cattle take their corn.

8.63.d: तद्दधाना अवस्यवो युष्माभिर्दक्षपितरः । स्याम मरुत्वतो वृधे ॥
8.63.e: Receiving this and craving help, we, who with you are Dakṣa's sons,  Would fain exalt the Maruts’ Lord.

8.63.d: बळृत्वियाय धाम्न ऋक्वभिः शूर नोनुमः । जेषामेन्द्र त्वया युजा ॥
8.63.e: Yea, Hero, with the singers we sing to the duly-coming Band Allied with thee may we prevail.

8.63.d: अस्मे रुद्रा मेहना पर्वतासो वृत्रहत्ये भरहूतौ सजोषाः । यः शंसते स्तुवते धायि पज्र इन्द्रज्येष्ठा अस्माँ अवन्तु देवाः ॥
8.63.e: With us are raining Rudras, clouds accordant in call to battle at the death of Vṛtra, The strong assigned to him who sings and praises. May Gods with Indra at their head protect us.

8.64.d: उत्त्वा मन्दन्तु स्तोमाः कृणुष्व राधो अद्रिवः । अव ब्रह्मद्विषो जहि ॥
8.64.e: MAY our hymns give thee great delight. Display thy bounty, Thunderer.  Drive off the enemies of prayer.

8.64.d: पदा पणीँरराधसो नि बाधस्व महाँ असि । नहि त्वा कश्चन प्रति ॥
8.64.e: Crush with thy foot the niggard churls who bring no gifts. Mighty art thou  There is not one to equal thee.

8.64.d: त्वमीशिषे सुतानामिन्द्र त्वमसुतानाम् । त्वं राजा जनानाम् ॥
8.64.e: Thou art the Lord of Soma pressed, Soma impressed is also thine.  Thou art the Sovran of the folk.

8.64.d: एहि प्रेहि क्षयो दिव्या३घोषञ्चर्षणीनाम् । ओभे पृणासि रोदसी ॥
8.64.e: Come, go thou forth, dwelling in heaven and listening to the prayers of men:  Thou fillest both the heavens and earth.

8.64.d: त्यं चित्पर्वतं गिरिं शतवन्तं सहस्रिणम् । वि स्तोतृभ्यो रुरोजिथ ॥
8.64.e: Even that hill with rocky heights, with hundreds, thousands, held within.  Thou for thy worshippers brakest through.

8.64.d: वयमु त्वा दिवा सुते वयं नक्तं हवामहे । अस्माकं काममा पृण ॥
8.64.e: We call on thee both night and day to taste the flowing Soma juice:  Do thou fulfil our heart's desire.

8.64.d: क्व१ स्य वृषभो युवा तुविग्रीवो अनानतः । ब्रह्मा कस्तं सपर्यति ॥
8.64.e: Where is that ever-youthful Steer, strong. necked and never yet bent down?  What Brahman ministers to him?

8.64.d: कस्य स्वित्सवनं वृषा जुजुष्वाँ अव गच्छति । इन्द्रं क उ स्विदा चके ॥
8.64.e: To whose libation doth the Steer, betake him with delight therein?  Who takes delight in Indra now?

8.64.d: कं ते दाना असक्षत वृत्रहन्कं सुवीर्या । उक्थे क उ स्विदन्तमः ॥
8.64.e: Whom, Vṛtra-slayer, have thy gifts and hero powers accompanied? Who is thy dearest in the land?

8.64.d: अयं ते मानुषे जने सोमः पूरुषु सूयते । तस्येहि प्र द्रवा पिब ॥
8.64.e: For thee among mankind, among the Pūrus is this Soma shed. Hasten thou hither: drink thereof.

8.64.d: अयं ते शर्यणावति सुषोमायामधि प्रियः । आर्जीकीये मदिन्तमः ॥
8.64.e: This, growing by Sushomā and by Śaryaṇāvān, dear to thee, in Ārjīkīya, cheers thee best.

8.64.d: तमद्य राधसे महे चारुं मदाय घृष्वये । एहीमिन्द्र द्रवा पिब ॥
8.64.e: Hasten thou hitherward, and drink this for munificence to-day Delightful for thine eager draught.

8.65.d: यदिन्द्र प्रागपागुदङ्न्यग्वा हूयसे नृभिः । आ याहि तूयमाशुभिः ॥
8.65.e: THOUGH, Indra, thou art called by men from east and west, from north and south,  Come hither quickly with fleet steeds

8.65.d: यद्वा प्रस्रवणे दिवो मादयासे स्वर्णरे । यद्वा समुद्रे अन्धसः ॥
8.65.e: If in the effluence of heaven, rich in its light, thou takest joy,  Or in the sea in Soma juice.

8.65.d: आ त्वा गीर्भिर्महामुरुं हुवे गामिव भोजसे । इन्द्र सोमस्य पीतये ॥
8.65.e: With songs I call thee, Great and Wide, even as a cow to profit us,  Indra, to drink the Soma-draught.

8.65.d: आ त इन्द्र महिमानं हरयो देव ते महः । रथे वहन्तु बिभ्रतः ॥
8.65.e: Hither, O Indra, let thy Bays bear up and, bring upon thy car  Thy glory, God! and majesty.

8.65.d: इन्द्र गृणीष उ स्तुषे महाँ उग्र ईशानकृत् । एहि नः सुतं पिब ॥
8.65.e: Thou, Indra, wouldst be sung and praised as great, strong, lordly in thy deeds  Come hither, drink our Soma juice.

8.65.d: सुतावन्तस्त्वा वयं प्रयस्वन्तो हवामहे । इदं नो बर्हिरासदे ॥
8.65.e: We who have shed the Soma and prepared the feast are calling thee.  To sit on this our sacred grass.

8.65.d: यच्चिद्धि शश्वतामसीन्द्र साधारणस्त्वम् । तं त्वा वयं हवामहे ॥
8.65.e: As, Indra, thou art evermore the common Lord of all alike,  As such we invocate thee now.

8.65.d: इदं ते सोम्यं मध्वधुक्षन्नद्रिभिर्नरः । जुषाण इन्द्र तत्पिब ॥
8.65.e: The men with stones have milked for thee this nectar of the Soma juice:  Indra, be pleased with it, and drink.

8.65.d: विश्वाँ अर्यो विपश्चितोऽति ख्यस्तूयमा गहि । अस्मे धेहि श्रवो बृहत् ॥
8.65.e: Neglect all pious men with skill in sacred song: come hitherward With speed, and give us high renown.

8.65.d: दाता मे पृषतीनां राजा हिरण्यवीनाम् । मा देवा मघवा रिषत् ॥
8.65.e: Gods, may the mighty rest unharmed, the King who gives spotted kine, Kine decked with golden ornaments.

8.65.d: सहस्रे पृषतीनामधि श्चन्द्रं बृहत्पृथु । शुक्रं हिरण्यमा ददे ॥
8.65.e: Beside a thousand spotted kine I have received a gift of gold Pure, brilliant, and exceeding great.

8.65.d: नपातो दुर्गहस्य मे सहस्रेण सुराधसः । श्रवो देवेष्वक्रत ॥
8.65.e: Durgaha’s grandsons, giving me a thousand kine, munificent Have won renown among the Gods.

8.66.d: तरोभिर्वो विदद्वसुमिन्द्रं सबाध ऊतये । बृहद्गायन्तः सुतसोमे अध्वरे हुवे भरं न कारिणम् ॥
8.66.e: LOUD singing at the sacred rite where Soma flows we priests invoke  With haste, that he may help, as the bard's Cherisher, Indra who findeth wealth for you.

8.66.d: न यं दुध्रा वरन्ते न स्थिरा मुरो मदे सुशिप्रमन्धसः । य आदृत्या शशमानाय सुन्वते दाता जरित्र उक्थ्यम् ॥
8.66.e: Whom with fair helm, in rapture of the juice, the firm resistless slayers hinder not:  Giver of glorious wealth to him who sing a his praise, honouring him who toils and pours:

8.66.d: यः शक्रो मृक्षो अश्व्यो यो वा कीजो हिरण्ययः । स ऊर्वस्य रेजयत्यपावृतिमिन्द्रो गव्यस्य वृत्रहा ॥
8.66.e: Śakra, who like a curry-comb for horses or a golden goad,  Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer, urges eagerly the opening of the stall of kine:

8.66.d: निखातं चिद्यः पुरुसम्भृतं वसूदिद्वपति दाशुषे । वज्री सुशिप्रो हर्यश्व इत्करदिन्द्रः क्रत्वा यथा वशत् ॥
8.66.e: Who for the worshipper scatters forth ample wealth, even though buried, piled in heaps:  May Indra, Lord of Bay Steeds, fair-helmed Thunderer, act at his pleasure, as he lists.

8.66.d: यद्वावन्थ पुरुष्टुत पुरा चिच्छूर नृणाम् । वयं तत्त इन्द्र सं भरामसि यज्ञमुक्थं तुरं वचः ॥
8.66.e: Hero whom many praise, what thou hast longed for, oven of old, from men.  All that we offer unto thee, O Indra, now, sacrifice, laud, effectual speech.

8.66.d: सचा सोमेषु पुरुहूत वज्रिवो मदाय द्युक्ष सोमपाः । त्वमिद्धि ब्रह्मकृते काम्यं वसु देष्ठः सुन्वते भुवः ॥
8.66.e: To Soma, Much-invoked, Bolt-armed! for thy carouse, Celestial, Soma-drinker! come. Thou to the man who prays and pours the juice hast been best giver of delightful wealth.

8.66.d: वयमेनमिदा ह्योऽपीपेमेह वज्रिणम् । तस्मा उ अद्य समना सुतं भरा नूनं भूषत श्रुते ॥
8.66.e: Here, verily, yesterday we let the Thunder-wielder drink his fill. So in like manner offer him the juice to-day. Now range you by the Glorious One.

8.66.d: वृकश्चिदस्य वारण उरामथिरा वयुनेषु भूषति । सेमं नः स्तोमं जुजुषाण आ गहीन्द्र प्र चित्रया धिया ॥
8.66.e: Even the wolf, the savage beast that rends the sheep, follows the path of his decrees. So graciously accepting, Indra, this our praise, with wondrous thought come forth to us.

8.66.d: कदू न्व१स्याकृतमिन्द्रस्यास्ति पौंस्यम् । केनो नु कं श्रोमतेन न शुश्रुवे जनुषः परि वृत्रहा ॥
8.66.e: What manly deed of vigour now remains that Indra hath not done? Who hath not heard his glorious title and his fame, the Vṛtra-slayer from his birth?

8.66.d: कदू महीरधृष्टा अस्य तविषीः कदु वृत्रघ्नो अस्तृतम् । इन्द्रो विश्वान्बेकनाटाँ अहर्दृश उत क्रत्वा पणीँरभि ॥
8.66.e: How great his power resistless! how invincible the Vṛtra-slayer’s matchless might! Indra excels all usurers who see the day, excels all traffickers in strength.

8.66.d: वयं घा ते अपूर्व्येन्द्र ब्रह्माणि वृत्रहन् । पुरूतमासः पुरुहूत वज्रिवो भृतिं न प्र भरामसि ॥
8.66.e: O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer, we, thy very constant worshippers, Bring prayers ne’er heard before to thee, O Much-invoked, O Thunder-armed, to be thy meed.

8.66.d: पूर्वीश्चिद्धि त्वे तुविकूर्मिन्नाशसो हवन्त इन्द्रोतयः । तिरश्चिदर्यः सवना वसो गहि शविष्ठ श्रुधि मे हवम् ॥
8.66.e: O thou of mighty acts, the aids that are in thee call forward many an eager hope. Past the drink-offerings, Vasu, even of the good, hear my call, Strongest God, and come.

8.66.d: वयं घा ते त्वे इद्विन्द्र विप्रा अपि ष्मसि । नहि त्वदन्यः पुरुहूत कश्चन मघवन्नस्ति मर्डिता ॥
8.66.e: Verily, Indra, we are thine, we worshippers depend on thee, For there is none but only thou to show us grace, O Maghavan, thou much invoked.

8.66.d: त्वं नो अस्या अमतेरुत क्षुधो३ऽभिशस्तेरव स्पृधि । त्वं न ऊती तव चित्रया धिया शिक्षा शचिष्ठ गातुवित् ॥
8.66.e: From this our misery and famine set us free, from this dire curse deliver us. Succour us with thine help and with thy wondrous thought, Most Mighty, finder of the way,

8.66.d: सोम इद्वः सुतो अस्तु कलयो मा बिभीतन । अपेदेष ध्वस्मायति स्वयं घैषो अपायति ॥
8.66.e: Now let your Soma juice be poured: be not afraid, O Kali's sons. This darkening sorrow goes away; yea, of itself it vanishes.

8.67.d: त्यान्नु क्षत्रियाँ अव आदित्यान्याचिषामहे । सुमृळीकाँ अभिष्टये ॥
8.67.e: Now pray we to these Ksatriyas, to the Ādityas for their aid,  These who are gracious to assist.

8.67.d: मित्रो नो अत्यंहतिं वरुणः पर्षदर्यमा । आदित्यासो यथा विदुः ॥
8.67.e: May Mitra bear us o’er distress, and Varuṇa and Aryaman,  Yea, the Ādityas, as they know.

8.67.d: तेषां हि चित्रमुक्थ्यं१ वरूथमस्ति दाशुषे । आदित्यानामरंकृते ॥
8.67.e: For wonderful and meet for praise is these Ādityas’ saving help  To him who offers and prepares.

8.67.d: महि वो महतामवो वरुण मित्रार्यमन् । अवांस्या वृणीमहे ॥
8.67.e: The mighty aid of you, the Great, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,  We claim to be our sure defence.

8.67.d: जीवान्नो अभि धेतनादित्यासः पुरा हथात् । कद्ध स्थ हवनश्रुतः ॥
8.67.e: Guard us, Ādityas, still alive, before the deadly weapon strike:  Are yc not they who hear our call?

8.67.d: यद्वः श्रान्ताय सुन्वते वरूथमस्ति यच्छर्दिः । तेना नो अधि वोचत ॥
8.67.e: What sheltering defence ye have for him who toils in pouring gifts, Graciously bless ye us therewith.

8.67.d: अस्ति देवा अंहोरुर्वस्ति रत्नमनागसः । आदित्या अद्भुतैनसः ॥
8.67.e: Ādityas, Gods, from sorrow there is freedom, for the sinless, wealth, O ye in whom no fault is seen.

8.67.d: मा नः सेतुः सिषेदयं महे वृणक्तु नस्परि । इन्द्र इद्धि श्रुतो वशी ॥
8.67.e: Let not this fetter bind us fast: may he release us for success; For strong is Indra and renowned.

8.67.d: मा नो मृचा रिपूणां वृजिनानामविष्यवः । देवा अभि प्र मृक्षत ॥
8.67.e: 0 Gods who fain would lend your aid, destroy not us as ye destroy Your enemies who go astray.

8.67.d: उत त्वामदिते मह्यहं देव्युप ब्रुवे । सुमृळीकामभिष्टये ॥
8.67.e: And thee too, O Great Aditi, thee also, Goddess, I address, Thee very gracious to assist.

8.67.d: पर्षि दीने गभीर आँ उग्रपुत्रे जिघांसतः । माकिस्तोकस्य नो रिषत् ॥
8.67.e: Save us in depth and shallow from the foe, thou Mother of Strong Sons: Let no one of our seed be harmed.

8.67.d: अनेहो न उरुव्रज उरूचि वि प्रसर्तवे । कृधि तोकाय जीवसे ॥
8.67.e: Far-spread! wide-ruling! grant that we, unharmed by envy may expand: Grant that our progeny may live.

8.67.d: ये मूर्धानः क्षितीनामदब्धासः स्वयशसः । व्रता रक्षन्ते अद्रुहः ॥
8.67.e: Those who, the Princes of the folk, in native glory, ne'er deceived, Maintain their statutes, void of guile —

8.67.d: ते न आस्नो वृकाणामादित्यासो मुमोचत । स्तेनं बद्धमिवादिते ॥
8.67.e: As such, from mouth of ravening wolves, O ye Ādityas, rescue us, Like a bound thief, O Aditi.

8.67.d: अपो षु ण इयं शरुरादित्या अप दुर्मतिः । अस्मदेत्वजघ्नुषी ॥
8.67.e: Ādityas, let this arrow, yea, let this malignity depart From us or e’er it strike us dead.

8.67.d: शश्वद्धि वः सुदानव आदित्या ऊतिभिर्वयम् । पुरा नूनं बुभुज्महे ॥
8.67.e: For, Bountiful Ādityas, we have evermore enjoyed your help, Both now and in the days of old.

8.67.d: शश्वन्तं हि प्रचेतसः प्रतियन्तं चिदेनसः । देवाः कृणुथ जीवसे ॥
8.67.e: To every one, O ye Most Wise, who turneth even from sin to you, Ye Gods vouchsafe that he may live.

8.67.d: तत्सु नो नव्यं सन्यस आदित्या यन्मुमोचति । बन्धाद्बद्धमिवादिते ॥
8.67.e: May this new mercy profit us, which, ye Ādityas, frees like one Bound from his bonds, O Aditi.

8.67.d: नास्माकमस्ति तत्तर आदित्यासो अतिष्कदे । यूयमस्मभ्यं मृळत ॥
8.67.e: O ye Ādityas, this your might is not to be despised by us: So be ye graciously inclined.

8.67.d: मा नो हेतिर्विवस्वत आदित्याः कृत्रिमा शरुः । पुरा नु जरसो वधीत् ॥
8.67.e: Let not Vivasvān’s weapon nor the shaft, Ādityas, wrought with skill, Destroy us ere old age be nigh.

8.67.d: वि षु द्वेषो व्यंहतिमादित्यासो वि संहितम् । विष्वग्वि वृहता रपः ॥
8.67.e: On every side dispel all sin, Ādityas, all hostility, Indigence, and combined attack.

8.68.d: आ त्वा रथं यथोतये सुम्नाय वर्तयामसि । तुविकूर्मिमृतीषहमिन्द्र शविष्ठ सत्पते ॥
8.68.e: EVEN as a car to give us aid, we draw thee hither for our bliss,  Strong in thy deeds, checking assault, Lord, Mightiest Indra, of the brave!

8.68.d: तुविशुष्म तुविक्रतो शचीवो विश्वया मते । आ पप्राथ महित्वना ॥
8.68.e: Great in thy power and wisdom, Strong, with thought that comprehendeth all  Thou hast filled full with majesty.

8.68.d: यस्य ते महिना महः परि ज्मायन्तमीयतुः । हस्ता वज्रं हिरण्ययम् ॥
8.68.e: Thou very Mighty One, whose hands by virtue of thy greatness grasp,  The golden bolt that breaks its way.

8.68.d: विश्वानरस्य वस्पतिमनानतस्य शवसः । एवैश्च चर्षणीनामूती हुवे रथानाम् ॥
8.68.e: Your Lord of might that ne’er hath bent, that ruleth over all mankind,  I call, that he, as he is wont, may aid the chariots and the men.

8.68.d: अभिष्टये सदावृधं स्वर्मीळ्हेषु यं नरः । नाना हवन्त ऊतये ॥
8.68.e: Whom, ever farthering, in frays that win the light, in both the hosts Men call to succour and to help.
Indra, the Strong, the measureless, worthy of praise, Most Bountiful, Sole Ruler even over wealth.

8.68.d: तंतमिद्राधसे मह इन्द्रं चोदामि पीतये । यः पूर्व्यामनुष्टुतिमीशे कृष्टीनां नृतुः ॥
8.68.e: Him, for his ample bounty, him, this Indra do I urge to drink, Who, as his praise was sung of old, the Dancer, is the Lord of men.

8.68.d: न यस्य ते शवसान सख्यमानंश मर्त्यः । नकिः शवांसि ते नशत् ॥
8.68.e: Thou Mighty One, whose friendship none of mortals ever hath obtained: None will attain unto thy might.

8.68.d: त्वोतासस्त्वा युजाप्सु सूर्ये महद्धनम् । जयेम पृत्सु वज्रिवः ॥
8.68.e: Aided by thee, with thee allied, in frays for water and for sun, Bolt-armed! may we win ample spoil.

8.68.d: तं त्वा यज्ञेभिरीमहे तं गीर्भिर्गिर्वणस्तम । इन्द्र यथा चिदाविथ वाजेषु पुरुमाय्यम् ॥
8.68.e: So seek we thee with sacrifice and songs, chief Lover of the Song, As, in our battles, Indra, thou to Purumāyya gavest help.

8.68.d: यस्य ते स्वादु सख्यं स्वाद्वी प्रणीतिरद्रिवः । यज्ञो वितन्तसाय्यः ॥
8.68.e: O Thunderer, thou whose friendship and whose Onward guidance both are sweet, Thy sacrifice must be prepared.

8.68.d: उरु णस्तन्वे३ तन उरु क्षयाय नस्कृधि । उरु णो यन्धि जीवसे ॥
8.68.e: To us, ourselves, give ample room, give for our dwelling ample room: Give ample room to us to live.

8.68.d: उरुं नृभ्य उरुं गव उरुं रथाय पन्थाम् । देववीतिं मनामहे ॥
8.68.e: We count the banquet of the Gods a spacious pathway for the men, And for the cattle, and the car.

8.68.d: उप मा षड्द्वाद्वा नरः सोमस्य हर्ष्या । तिष्ठन्ति स्वादुरातयः ॥
8.68.e: Six men, yea, two and two, made glad with Soma juice, come near to me With offerings pleasant to the taste.

8.68.d: ऋज्राविन्द्रोत आ ददे हरी ऋक्षस्य सूनवि । आश्वमेधस्य रोहिता ॥
8.68.e: Two brown-hued steeds, Indrota’s gift, two bays from Ṛkṣa’s son were mine, From Asvamedha’s son two red.
From Atithigva good car-steeds, from Arksha rein-obeying steeds, From Asvamedha beauteous ones.

8.68.d: षळश्वाँ आतिथिग्व इन्द्रोते वधूमतः । सचा पूतक्रतौ सनम् ॥
8.68.e: Indrota, Atithigva’s son, gave me six horses matched with mares: And Putakratu gave besides.
Marked above all, amid the brown, is the red mare Vṛshaṇvatī, Obedient to the rein and whip.

8.68.d: न युष्मे वाजबन्धवो निनित्सुश्चन मर्त्यः । अवद्यमधि दीधरत् ॥
8.68.e: O bound to me by deeds of might, not even the man who loves to blame Hath found a single fault in you.

8.69.d: प्रप्र वस्त्रिष्टुभमिषं मन्दद्वीरायेन्दवे । धिया वो मेधसातये पुरंध्या विवासति ॥
8.69.e: I SEND you forth the song of praise for Indu, hero-gladdener.  With hymn and plenty he invites you to complete the sacrifice.

8.69.d: नदं व ओदतीनां नदं योयुवतीनाम् । पतिं वो अघ्न्यानां धेनूनामिषुध्यसि ॥
8.69.e: Thou wishest for thy kine a bull, for those who long for his approach,  For those who turn away from him, lord of thy cows whom none may kill.

8.69.d: ता अस्य सूददोहसः सोमं श्रीणन्ति पृश्नयः । जन्मन्देवानां विशस्त्रिष्वा रोचने दिवः ॥
8.69.e: The dappled kine who stream with milk prepare his draught of Soma juice:  Clans in the birth-place of the Gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.

8.69.d: अभि प्र गोपतिं गिरेन्द्रमर्च यथा विदे । सूनुं सत्यस्य सत्पतिम् ॥
8.69.e: Praise, even as he is known, with song Indra the guardian of the kine, The Son of Truth, Lord of the brave.

8.69.d: आ हरयः ससृज्रिरेऽरुषीरधि बर्हिषि । यत्राभि संनवामहे ॥
8.69.e: Hither his Bay Steeds have been sent, red Steeds are on the sacred grass Where we in concert sing our songs.

8.69.d: इन्द्राय गाव आशिरं दुदुह्रे वज्रिणे मधु । यत्सीमुपह्वरे विदत् ॥
8.69.e: For Indra Thunder-armed the kine have yielded mingled milk and meath, What time he found them in the vault.

8.69.d: उद्यद्ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपं गृहमिन्द्रश्च गन्वहि । मध्वः पीत्वा सचेवहि त्रिः सप्त सख्युः पदे ॥
8.69.e: When I and Indra mount on high up to the Bright One’s place and home, We, having drunk of meath, will reach his seat whose Friends are three times seven.

8.69.d: अर्चत प्रार्चत प्रियमेधासो अर्चत । अर्चन्तु पुत्रका उत पुरं न धृष्ण्वर्चत ॥
8.69.e: Sing, sing ye forth your songs of praise, ye Priyamedhas, sing your songs: Yea, let young children sing their lauds: as a strong castle praise ye him.

8.69.d: अव स्वराति गर्गरो गोधा परि सनिष्वणत् । पिङ्गा परि चनिष्कददिन्द्राय ब्रह्मोद्यतम् ॥
8.69.e: Now loudly let the viol sound, the lute send out its voice with might, Shrill be the music of the string. To Indra is the hymn upraised

8.69.d: आ यत्पतन्त्येन्यः सुदुघा अनपस्फुरः । अपस्फुरं गृभायत सोममिन्द्राय पातवे ॥
8.69.e: When hither speed the dappled cows, unflinching, easy to be milked, Seize quickly, as it bursts away, the Soma juice for Indra’s drink

8.69.d: अपादिन्द्रो अपादग्निर्विश्वे देवा अमत्सत । वरुण इदिह क्षयत्तमापो अभ्यनूषत वत्सं संशिश्वरीरिव ॥
8.69.e: Indra hath drunk, Agni hath drunk: all Deities have drunk their fill. Here VARUNA shall have his home, to whom the floods have sung aloud as mother-kine unto their calves.

8.69.d: सुदेवो असि वरुण यस्य ते सप्त सिन्धवः । अनुक्षरन्ति काकुदं सूर्म्यं सुषिरामिव ॥
8.69.e: Thou, VARUNA, to whom belong Seven Rivers, art a glorious God. The waters flow into thy throat as 'twere a pipe with ample mouth.

8.69.d: यो व्यतीँरफाणयत्सुयुक्ताँ उप दाशुषे । तक्वो नेता तदिद्वपुरुपमा यो अमुच्यत ॥
8.69.e: He who hath made the fleet steeds spring, well-harnessed, to the worshipper, He, the swift Guide, is that fair form that loosed the horses near at hand.

8.69.d: अतीदु शक्र ओहत इन्द्रो विश्वा अति द्विषः । भिनत्कनीन ओदनं पच्यमानं परो गिरा ॥
8.69.e: Indra, the very Mighty, holds his enemies in utter scorn. He, far away, and yet a child, cleft the cloud smitten by his voice.

8.69.d: अर्भको न कुमारकोऽधि तिष्ठन्नवं रथम् । स पक्षन्महिषं मृगं पित्रे मात्रे विभुक्रतुम् ॥
8.69.e: He, yet a boy exceeding small, mounted his newly-fashioned car. He for his Mother and his Sire cooked the wild mighty buffalo.

8.69.d: आ तू सुशिप्र दम्पते रथं तिष्ठा हिरण्ययम् । अध द्युक्षं सचेवहि सहस्रपादमरुषं स्वस्तिगामनेहसम् ॥
8.69.e: Lord of the home, fair-helmeted, ascend thy chariot wrought of gold. We will attend the Heavenly One, the thousand-footed, red of hue, matchless, who blesses where he goes.

8.69.d: तं घेमित्था नमस्विन उप स्वराजमासते । अर्थं चिदस्य सुधितं यदेतव आवर्तयन्ति दावने ॥
8.69.e: With reverence they come hitherward to him as to a Sovran Lord, That they may bring him near for this man’s good success, to prosper and bestow his gifts.

8.69.d: अनु प्रत्नस्यौकसः प्रियमेधास एषाम् । पूर्वामनु प्रयतिं वृक्तबर्हिषो हितप्रयस आशत ॥
8.69.e: The Priyamedhas have observed the offering of the men of old, of ancient custom, while they strewed the sacred grass, and spread their sacrificial food.

8.70.d: यो राजा चर्षणीनां याता रथेभिरध्रिगुः । विश्वासां तरुता पृतनानां ज्येष्ठो यो वृत्रहा गृणे ॥
8.70.e: HE who, as Sovran Lord of men, moves with his chariots unrestrained,  The Vṛtra-slayer vanquisher, of fighting hosts, preeminent, is praised with song.

8.70.d: इन्द्रं तं शुम्भ पुरुहन्मन्नवसे यस्य द्विता विधर्तरि । हस्ताय वज्रः प्रति धायि दर्शतो महो दिवे न सूर्यः ॥
8.70.e: Honour that Indra, Puruhanman! for his aid, in whose sustaining hand of old,  The splendid bolt of thunder was deposited, as the great Sun was set in heaven.

8.70.d: नकिष्टं कर्मणा नशद्यश्चकार सदावृधम् । इन्द्रं न यज्ञैर्विश्वगूर्तमृभ्वसमधृष्टं धृष्ण्वोजसम् ॥
8.70.e: No one by deed attains to him who works and strengthens evermore:  No, not by sacrifice, to Indra. praised o all, resistless, daring, bold in might.

8.70.d: अषाळ्हमुग्रं पृतनासु सासहिं यस्मिन्महीरुरुज्रयः । सं धेनवो जायमाने अनोनवुर्द्यावः क्षामो अनोनवुः ॥
8.70.e: The potent Conqueror, invincible in war, him at whose birth the Mighty Ones,  The Kine who spread  afar  , sent their loud voices out, heavens, earths seat their loud voices out,

8.70.d: यद्द्याव इन्द्र ते शतं शतं भूमीरुत स्युः । न त्वा वज्रिन्त्सहस्रं सूर्या अनु न जातमष्ट रोदसी ॥
8.70.e: O Indra, if a hundred heavens and if a hundred earths were thine—  No, not a thousand Suns could match thee at thy birth, not both the worlds, O Thunderer.

8.70.d: आ पप्राथ महिना वृष्ण्या वृषन्विश्वा शविष्ठ शवसा । अस्माँ अव मघवन्गोमति व्रजे वज्रिञ्चित्राभिरूतिभिः ॥
8.70.e: Thou, Hero, hast performed thy hero deeds with might, yea, all with strength, O Strongest One.  Maghavan, help us to a stable full of kine, O Thunderer, with wondrous aids.

8.70.d: न सीमदेव आपदिषं दीर्घायो मर्त्यः । एतग्वा चिद्य एतशा युयोजते हरी इन्द्रो युयोजते ॥
8.70.e: Let not a godless mortal gain this food, O thou whose life is long!  But one who yokes the bright-hued steeds, the Etasas, even Indra yoker of the Bays.

8.70.d: तं वो महो महाय्यमिन्द्रं दानाय सक्षणिम् । यो गाधेषु य आरणेषु हव्यो वाजेष्वस्ति हव्यः ॥
8.70.e: Urge ye the Conqueror to give, your Indra greatly to be praised, To be invoked in shallow waters and in depths, to be invoked in deeds of might.

8.70.d: उदू षु णो वसो महे मृशस्व शूर राधसे । उदू षु मह्यै मघवन्मघत्तय उदिन्द्र श्रवसे महे ॥
8.70.e: O Vasu, O thou Hero, raise us up to ample opulence. Raise us to gain of mighty wealth, O Maghavan, O Indra, to sublime renown.

8.70.d: त्वं न इन्द्र ऋतयुस्त्वानिदो नि तृम्पसि । मध्ये वसिष्व तुविनृम्णोर्वोर्नि दासं शिश्नथो हथैः ॥
8.70.e: Indra, thou justifiest us, and tramplest down thy slanderers. Guard thyself, valiant Hero, in thy vital parts: strike down the Dāsa with thy blows.

8.70.d: अन्यव्रतममानुषमयज्वानमदेवयुम् । अव स्वः सखा दुधुवीत पर्वतः सुघ्नाय दस्युं पर्वतः ॥
8.70.e: The man who brings no sacrifice, inhuman, godless, infidel, Him let his friend the mountain cast to rapid death, the mountain cast the Dasyu down.

8.70.d: त्वं न इन्द्रासां हस्ते शविष्ठ दावने । धानानां न सं गृभायास्मयुर्द्विः सं गृभायास्मयुः ॥
8.70.e: O Mightiest Indra, loving us, gather thou up, as grains of corn Within thine hand, of these their kine, to give away, yea, gather twice as loving us.

8.70.d: सखायः क्रतुमिच्छत कथा राधाम शरस्य । उपस्तुतिं भोजः सूरिर्यो अह्रयः ॥
8.70.e: O my companions, wish for power. How may we perfect Saras praise, The liberal princely patron, never to be harmed?

8.70.d: भूरिभिः समह ऋषिभिर्बर्हिष्मद्भिः स्तविष्यसे । यदित्थमेकमेकमिच्छर वत्सान्पराददः ॥
8.70.e: By many a sage whose grass is trimmed thou art continually praised, That thou, O Ṣara, hast bestowed here one and here another calf.

8.70.d: कर्णगृह्या मघवा शौरदेव्यो वत्सं नस्त्रिभ्य आनयत् । अजां सूरिर्न धातवे ॥
8.70.e: The noble, Ṣūradeva’s son, hath brought a calf, led by the ear, to three of us, As a chief brings a goat to milk.

8.71.d: त्वं नो अग्ने महोभिः पाहि विश्वस्या अरातेः । उत द्विषो मर्त्यस्य ॥
8.71.e: O AGNI, with thy mighty wealth guard us from all malignity, Yea, from all hate of mortal man.

8.71.d: नहि मन्युः पौरुषेय ईशे हि वः प्रियजात । त्वमिदसि क्षपावान् ॥
8.71.e: For over thee, O Friend from birth, the wrath of man hath no control: Nay, Guardian of the earth art thou.

8.71.d: स नो विश्वेभिर्देवेभिरूर्जो नपाद्भद्रशोचे । रयिं देहि विश्ववारम् ॥
8.71.e: As such, with all the Gods, O Son of Strength, auspicious in thy flame. Give us wealth bringing all things good.

8.71.d: न तमग्ने अरातयो मर्तं युवन्त रायः । यं त्रायसे दाश्वांसम् ॥
8.71.e: Malignities stay not from wealth the mortal man whom, Agni, thou Protectest while he offers gifts.

8.71.d: यं त्वं विप्र मेधसातावग्ने हिनोषि धनाय । स तवोती गोषु गन्ता ॥
8.71.e: Sage Agni, be whom thou dost urge, in worship of the Gods, to wealth, With thine assistance winneth kine.

8.71.d: त्वं रयिं पुरुवीरमग्ने दाशुषे मर्ताय । प्र णो नय वस्यो अच्छ ॥
8.71.e: Riches with many heroes thou hast for the man who offers gifts: Lead thou us on to higher bliss.

8.71.d: उरुष्या णो मा परा दा अघायते जातवेदः । दुराध्ये३ मर्ताय ॥
8.71.e: Save us, O Jātavedas, nor abandon us to him who sins, Unto the evil-hearted man.

8.71.d: अग्ने माकिष्टे देवस्य रातिमदेवो युयोत । त्वमीशिषे वसूनाम् ॥
8.71.e: O Agni, let no godless man avert thy bounty as a God: Over all treasures thou art Lord.

8.71.d: स नो वस्व उप मास्यूर्जो नपान्माहिनस्य । सखे वसो जरितृभ्यः ॥
8.71.e: So, Son of Strength, thou aidest us to what is great and excellent. Those, Vasu! Friend! who sing thy praise.

8.71.d: अच्छा नः शीरशोचिषं गिरो यन्तु दर्शतम् । अच्छा यज्ञासो नमसा पुरूवसुं पुरुप्रशस्तमूतये ॥
